The '''abysmal whip''' is a [[power level]] 4 one-handed melee weapon that can be created at a [[blacksmith's bench]]. The recipe, [[Abyssal Remains]], can be acquired by killing an [[Abyssal Demon]]. It can be ascended at a [[mystic forge]] with [[ascension core]]s. Note, if you ascend the Abysmal Whip to power level 8, and upgrade it to the [[Abyssal Whip]], it will be brought down to Power Level 7.

This weapon's [[special effect]] is that regular attacks also build up [[bleed]], and after five rapid hits, it will proc 28 damage at [[power level]] 4 and 40 damage at [[power level]] 7, despite only listing 25 for each. As this weapon deals slash damage, compared to swords, its attacks are slightly slower but slightly harder; however, its forward lunge distance is much shorter, and since enemies are knocked back significantly by most attacks, they will often be knocked out of this weapon's combos. It also does not have increased block without a shield compared to other similar weapons.

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|
We've all heard of it. We've all wanted it... the Legendary Abyssal Whip! The fabled weapon that heroes and adventurers have been seeking for an age!

You have taken it one step further. You have asked the question, "How hard could it be to make your own?". All you need is a spine from an Abyssal Demon! It comes pre-segmented and it's made from some of the hardiest organic material known to mortalkind. You just need to kill the demon, twist the shoulder, sever a tendon, and Io - your very own Abyssal Whip... right? Wrong. 

Turns out, it's a bit more involved than you expected, and this "weapon" demonstrates that all too well.

Still, not all is lost. Perhaps there is a way, a method, to turn this... "thing" into something that lives up to it's legend.
}}

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|
The abyssal demon is a foul beast. A single one can massacre a village before the warning bell can even sound. Crafting a weapon from their remains symbolizes triumph against adversity or perhaps just hubris in its purest form. 

Infused with the hate of the demon, each whip crack generates unbearable pain. Victims find themselves overcome with suffering as the agony seeps into the wounds the whips leave behind.

It is said that the whip even feeds on that misery, growing stronger with each life taken. The hate imbues the weapon with a desire to inflict more pain, and it grows stronger each time such a wish is granted. Or, so the legends say.

Only one Wild Knight has ever chosen to wield the whip in vengeance against the demon for a fallen sibling. Her name is dust in the wind of history, but there are still creatures that hide in the shadows, afraid of the crack of her whip.
}}

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|
Long ago, there were people in Ashenfall. Not humans, not elves, nor anyone you might remember, but sentient beings with a life, a culture and a civilisation all of their own. No trace of them remains today.

More and more of the Kobalios began to take more than their fair share. The Wellspring was never-ending, but it would only release at a steady rate. Only so much could be consumed at any one time, and fewer and fewer of the Kobalios were able to enjoy it.

In their desperation, they used rituals and spells to draw more anima from the Wellspring than it gave, and this caused a tiny crack to appear in the skein of creation. From this crack, smoke rose and filled the bellies of the greediest of the Kobalios.

The effect of the smoke was subtle, but deadly. It left a hole in the heart of the infected that made them yearn for more and more anima; to feast deeper and deeper upon the Wellspring, regardless of how it might impact their kin.
}}

'''Armour''' describes items worn in the head, chest, leg, or cape slot to defend against damage from melee, ranged, or magic-based attacks. ==Shields==
Shields are equipped in the off-hand and allow players to block and [[parry]] incoming attacks.

* Blocking reduces the incoming damage from the attack of a monster by the block value of the equipped shield.
* Parrying is when the beginning of a block coincides with the timing of an attack of a monster.  An audible "clang" will sound, and the enemy becomes staggered as long as they are not immune (e.g., [[Velgar]]).

'''Ascension cores''' are items used and crafted in the [[mystic forge]] to ascend masterwork weapons from their base power level to the next tier. They are made by combining [[ascension shard]]s or by collecting them as rewards for completing [[Nightmare Crucible]] instances in [[Umbral Sands]]. For most cores, players can gain core shards by killing mini-bosses (such as [[red dragon]]s, [[green dragon]]s, and [[blue dragon]]s).

The only core that ''cannot'' be crafted thus far is the power level 7 ascension core, which can only be acquired by completing the [[Nightmare Crucible]].

{{Journal entry|
Imagine, if you will, what you could do if you could harness your dreams. If you could take an ideal, refine it and reforge it using the power of the imagination. Such a technology is terrifying in its potential, and Avisk was the first to explore its possibilities.

This core is a part of the nightmare, refined and reforged over and over again, then condescended into a singularity and sealed within dragonkin technology. It is a mote of potential, waiting to be released.

The technology is limited for now. [[Avisk]] was only able to use it to improve his existing equipment, as well as to empower the beasts he trapped in the nightmare dreamscape. Fortunately, limited as it might be, you should find this technology particularly useful, as it will allow you upgrade and improve some of your more unique equipment, such as masterwork gear.

The '''bed''' is a buildable piece of [[Buildings#Furniture|furniture]] used to [[rest]] and set the player's respawn point in the world. If used at night, players will skip to daytime and regain their full rest meter; if used during the day, players will lie in place and slowly regain their rest meter over time. The bed requires 8 ash planks and 4 rough cloth to craft, and must be under a [[roof]] and enclosed with three [[wall]]s to be used.

Placing and claiming this bed will offer a "bonus" radius of 20m, preventing [[monsters]] from spawning within this area.{{fact}}

==Attacks==
* Lunge
* Tail sweep (if behind them)
* Fire Claw Slash
* Poison Blast: The black dragon launches a fire projectile to build up around the three-quarters point.
* Fire Breath: The black dragon sweeps the area in front of them with their fire breath.
* Wing Attack: The black dragon flaps its wings, blowing wind at the player, with the second such blast doing damage.
* Fly: The black dragon can fly into the sky and do a few moves:
** Fire Breath: The black dragon shoots their breath in a line going away from them. This staggers the player and can easily lock them in to take all of the damage.

{{external|rs=Black Knights' Fortress (quest)|os=Black Knights' Fortress|rsc=Black knight's fortress}} {{Infobox Quest | name = Black Knight's Fortress | image = Black Knight's Fortress.png | release = 31 March 2026 | update = 0.11 is live now! Enter Dowdun Reach... | series = Kuldra's Saga }}'''Black Knight's Fortress''' is the seventh primary [[Quests|quest]] and the third in the main storyline of ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds''. In this quest, the [[Player Character|Player]] must delve into an ancient mountainous fortress after defeating the revenant dragon [[Imaru]] in order to gain access to the [[Umbral Sands]]. == Quest Overview == {{Quest details|desc=Uncover the secrets of Dowdun Reach in order to unlock your way through to the Umbral Sands.|enemies=* Multiple [[Black Knights]] * Multiple [[mage of Zamorak]] * Multiple [[hellhound]]s * Four (different location) [[shardbound lesser demon]]s * [[Lesser demon]] * [[Blue dragon]] * [[Black Knight Titan]]|item_req=* Steel or Undead Spade * Steel or Mithril Pickaxe * Mithril Logging Axe * Fishing Rod (Any, preferably highest available)|qtype=primary|rec=* Good [[food]], potions * Good armour|req=* [[Withering Heights]] * Level 41 [[Cooking]] to cook [[maple sap]] into [[maple syrup]], or a [[maple toastie]] from a food [[salvage]] spot (1/24)|start=Speak to Death in the Forgotten Temple.}} == Walkthrough == === Part I: The Dark Fortress... === {{Map|Ominous Door|height=250px|width=250px|center=-351.45294,210897.64|float=right}} Speak to [[Death (Grim Reaper)|Death]] in the Forgotten Temple. He will mention about how you did well in Fellhollow, but that there is more for you to do. A colleague of his is waiting for you in the [[Umbral Sands]] to help him, but instructs you to speak to Cathan to gather allies and investigate. You can find Cathan east of Fellhollow, near the ominous gatehouse in the south of [[Silverthorn Keep]]. Speak to Cathan, who greets you, and he will comment about how the adventure never ends. He will then right to it and explain how he has been investigating the ominous gatehouse and, while it leads to some fortress, it is blocking the way to the Umbral Sands. He tells you how he wanted to scout out the place more all spooky-like, but made the mistake of mentioning it to the [[Wise Old Man]]. Knowing how he is like, Cathan mentioned about how he murmured some stuff like "amateur hour wards" and "rubbish defences" before storming down the passageway. Cathan will inform you that, if you want to go after him, to look for him in some sort of central point (like a nexus or something). Go through the open gateway and enter through the '''ominous door''' (Image right). '''Note:''' ''This will play a small intro cutscene to the area''. You will then arrive within [[The Approach]]. Traverse southward through this new region until you enter [[The Courtyard]] where you will meet the Wise Old Man. === Part II: Shadows Within === Speak to the Wise Old Man, who will mention about how you had an easier time getting here than they did and walloping a few troublesome people. He'd then mention about how he was hoping to hunt down another dragon to whittle down Kuldra's forces, but complains about the fortress full of Zamorakians in the way. Despite the bothersome trouble in the way, he mentions how great it is that you're here to help get them moving again. Troubling thing is, he mentions how the way is blocked by someone called "the gatekeeper" and he isn't sure who or what it may be. Despite not being aware of who or what it is, the Wise Old Man tells you that [[Doric]] is currently working on dispelling a nasty magical barrier further ahead in the Nexus. He then says how it might be a good idea to make a base camp here first. After making a base camp, follow the path leading up into the fortress. Arrive at [[The Nexus]] and speak to Doric. Once you speak to him, he will mention about how crazed the Black Knights are along with how they look like they should have all died long ago. He mentions how the problem is that you are all stuck here and he has everything to get the door open. As far as Doric can tell, everything seems to be connected to a [[Avisk|great big stone]] next to him. He says that it looks broken and, theorising a way to get past the door, might need to fix it using some missing pieces. Inspect the stone. This will reveal a small dialogue from the stone itself describing how it is broken, shards of itself are missing, and that you should find the missing pieces to repair it. It will then give you authorisation to look around the keep and to access the [[Nodestone|Nexus nodes]] scattered around [[Dowdun Reach]]. === Part III: Shard Hunting === '''Item(s) needed:''' ''Spade, Pickaxe, Logging Axe.''[[File:Shard Map Locations.png|thumb|width=405x405|The locations for the Shards of Dreaming Stone]] [[File:Underground Entrance.png|thumb|Follow arrow past all the Hellrat pens and turn left. Follow the staircase down to the lowest level. Explore this underground region for the three Shards of the Dreaming Stone.]] [[File:Underground Entrance2.png|thumb|Second entrance to underground region.]] After inspecting the Dreaming Stone, you will discover that there are thirteen [[Shard of the Dreaming Stone|shards]] (marked on your map with yellow circles) that are needed to repair it. These shards are scattered throughout Dowdun Reach and require you to either interact with characters, scenery objects, or solve puzzles to acquire them. While most are above-ground, there are three that are kept underground. Once you have collected all thirteen shards, head back to the Dreaming Stone. ====[[The Cathedral]]==== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !Location !Interact Type !Details |- |South-West |Cut down vines w/ mithril logging axe then standard interact |You can acquire the cathedral shard by heading south-west to a courtyard full of Zamorakian acolytes and mages and, using your mithril (or above) logging axe, cut down the vines. As the mages and acolytes are hostile by default, you will need to take them down first. |} ====[[The Garrison]]==== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !Location !Interact Type !Details |- |East |Defeat [[Sergeant Blister]] |He is located underground in The Garrison region, protected by two hellhounds and a small host of skeletons. The requirements to interact/collect this shard are the same as defeating the shardbound lesser demons. |- |West |Standard interact |Navigate past the elite Black Knight and two Zamorakian acolytes to an open wall with some wooden boards. Use the [[Windstep]] spell to jump up and across to the nearby adjacent tower. Once you have arrived, either defeat or avoid the elite Black Knight to interact with the shard. |} ====[[The Grand Hall]]==== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !Location !Interact Type !Details |- |East |Interact with [[Spittletoe]] |Spittletoe instructs you to collect five Maple Sap. Once you provide the sap, Spittletoe will trade you the shard. |} {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" ! Grand Hall shard steps |- | {{Checklist| *Speak with [[Spittletoe]] Speak with Spittletoe, while having the [[maple sap]] in your inventory. Continue dialogue until you receive a shard.
'''Note:''' When interacting with Spittletoe in the kitchen, it is possible for the Zogre to aggro the player from above, even without being in line of sight. If you do not have the maple sap, look for [[maple tree]]s and chop them down till you get one }} |} ====[[The Library]]==== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !Location !Interact Type !Details |- |North-West |Defeat 2x [[shardbound lesser demon]] |Open the library door by interacting with (in order) the following books: # The Empty Throne # The Eye of Oculus # Taking the Crown # Zamorak's Rebellion '''Note:''' You can make it easier to take them down by leading them into the spiral staircase. Despite the player needing to interact with the doorway to phase through, the lesser demons can walk through the doorway as if it is not there. |- |South-West |Interact with [[Valerius]] |Go to the top of the staircase (a floor above where Valerius can be found) and West, past the [[blue dragon]], and veer right as soon as you pass under the cliff. Equip your spade and dig in front of the gargoyle statue to uncover the [[glass owl]]. Return this item to Valerius to acquire this shard. |} ====[[The Menagerie]]==== [[File:Image 2026-04-01 185845116.png|thumb|Location of the gargoyle in the Menagerie/Library Region, West of the Blue Dragon.]] {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !Location !Interact type !Details |- |South | * Dig with spade * Cut down vines w/ mithril logging axe |Find three levers to unlock the door. The first lever is inside of the broken down roof of the tiny house (located next to the windmill). You'll need to cast Windstep to reach the roof, then use your spade here to dig it up and interact with it. The second lever is inside of a cave nearby protected by a thorny vine wall along the rock wall to the right of the shard. You will need a mithril or better logging axe to chop these vines. The third and final lever is on the top level of the nearby stone ruins, located beside the air anima vent. You'll need to use [[Windstep]] to reach this level. This area is guarded by a lesser blue dragon. |- |South-East |Standard interact |Follow along the lower area cliffs to reach an area where you can jump across. You'll also locate a group of hellhounds on your way there, but you can either ignore them or defeat them until you locate a series of beams. Traverse the beams by jumping up to the next level until you reach the top where you'll need to jump across to the stone rock where the shard is located. '''Note:''' You'll need plenty of air runes to use Windstep for this particular jumping puzzle. An alternative way is to equip your [[leggings of lightness]] and use Windstep from where you received the previous shard from finding the three levers, down to the cliffs. Be sure '''not''' to jump and head down, instead, fall with the spell and the leggings to avoid damage. |} ====[[The Pastures]]==== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !Location !Interact Type !Details |- |North |Mine a [[granite deposit]] |Reach the highest part of the goblin-infested fortress. In the middle of the area, there is a granite deposit that hides the shard. You can either avoid or defeat the blue dragon here to get to the shard, but you can use the [[Rocksplosion]] spell to quickly interact with the shard. |- |East |Interact button |Defeat the goblins in the immediate area of the shard before interacting with it. |} ====Underground Shards==== These are located underground, they can be completed in any order. =====[[The Crypt]] (underground)===== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !Location !Interact Type !Details |- |The Crypt |Dig with spade/shovel |Navigate to The Crypt in the underground region. Before searching for the shard, defeat the zogre here. This will save you trouble later. Interact with the [[Hastily Scrawled Note|note]] next to the goblin corpse to learn that the shard is buried in a grave. Dig at ''any'' of the graves until you uncover the shard. '''Note:''' ''The location of this shard is randomized for every world''. |} =====[[The Demon Gate]] (underground)===== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !Location !Interact Type !Details |- |The demon gate |Defeat 2x [[shardbound lesser demon]] |Navigate to the lowest part of the region. There is a lever-activated elevator that will take you down to the demon gate region. For easier traversal later, interact with the nearby nodestone to connect it to the Nexus. Navigate through the pathways until you reach the stone structure and defeat the two lesser demons guarding the shard. |} =====[[The Lake]] (underground)===== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !Location !Interact Type !Details |- |The Lake |Speak with [[Offalfoot]] |He will ask you to give him one of the fish nearby (requires an empty inventory slot), so you'll need to grab one from the nearby pool of fish. This will give you an [[unusual trout]] and give this trout to Offalfoot. He'll give you the shard. '''Note:''' You do need a fishing rod (the highest level is recommended) and this can be done with level 1 Fishing. You will encounter [[Delrom]] when traversing to through this location. |} === Part IV: Remember the Titans === Interact with the Dreaming Stone. It will say that it is restored, but it will reveal that it was evil! It will claim that its name will rattle in your tiny skull like the echoes within a cave. The Dreaming Stone then reveals its name to be '''Avisk the eternal''' whose mind had ever graced the Aughra, but as it tries to enslave you and become its thrall, it seemed stunned. This will reveal two dialogue options (both of which are about destroying the stone), but choose option one. This will force the crystal to acknowledge your logic and, in its own way, apologise for being overzealous and how it happens when you've been alone in the psyche of Black Knights for too long. It then blames the Cthonian before taking down the barrier. It then warns you to be wary of Lord Rasmodel (aka the [[Black Knight Titan]]) as it had a bit of a mishap when he smashed the Dreaming Stone to pieces. Now, he's got some of the Dreaming Stone , some of a demon, and a whole lot of anger issues. End the dialogue and the Dreaming Stone will be fully repaired. Interact with the newly-dropped Barrier and you'll arrive in [[The Bastion]]. Head up all the stairs (be mindful of some gaps which can be Windstepped) until you reach the top. Enter into the Bastion building and, just past a barrier, slay the boss. Interact with the barrier to fight the Titan. After defeating him, return to the Dreaming Stone. '''Note:''' The barrier may not allow you to teleport through if you have not unblocked all of the [[nodestone]]s; with the exception of The Bastion. === Part V: To the Umbral Sands! === Talk to the Dreaming Stone/Avsik. It will remark how impressive it was that you slew the Titan and that when he finds himself a new body to walk among the world again, he'd like for you to work with him. Aside from that, he remarks about how the gate to the Umbral Sands hasn't been opened in a long time, so he'll need time to get it unstuck. He also pleads for you to be patient - and to stay your hammer - as he will help get you into the desert soon. He then gives you a reward (read: bribe) for not smashing him to pieces with your hammer. '''Congratulations! Quest Complete!''' == Rewards == * 1x [[Black Knight's Fortress reward pack]] ** 1x [[Tome of the Titan]] *** +750 XP to Magic, Ranged, and Attack ** 1x [[Titan's wrath]] *Recipe to creating the [[Titan's wrath]] 2h sword ==Transcript== {{Hastranscript|quest}} == Required to Complete == ''This quest is required to complete the following:'' * [[Icthlarin's Little Helper]] == Trivia == * The quest's name is inspired by ''{{RSL|RuneScape}}'s'' and ''{{OSL|Old School RuneScape}}'s'' variant of the quest. ** In ''RuneScape'' the quest was replaced by {{RSL|The Death of Chivalry}} on 13 August 2013. *It is the third quest in the game's Early Access, also known as Kuldra's Saga. {{Black Knight's Fortress}} {{Quests}}

{{Game mechanics}}
[[Category:Construction]]
Buildings/Mechanics:
{{otheruses|the mechanics on how to create structures|the list of structures|Buildings}}
'''Building mechanics''' are ways that players can create [[building]] structures/objects, general decorations, and other types of furniture. Players can start building by pressing the default {{Key press|B}} button on their keyboard to unlock the building interface. 

[[File:BuildMenu Home.png|thumb|right|The home building interface.]]

==Placement==
[[File:Building mechanics (damaged wall).png|thumb|right|150px|A damaged cabin wall below 50% health on the bottom, compared to a regular wall at the top.]]
Upon clicking on an unlocked type of structure, players can choose the area to place the object and can rotate it as the object is previewed (assuming players have the required materials). Players can rotate the previewed structure with the following:
{| class="wikitable"
|+
!Key press
!Direction
|-
|Scroll wheel
|Rotation along the Z-axis
|-
|Alt + scroll wheel
|Towards/away from the player
|-
|Shift + scroll wheel
|Up/down from the world's surface
|}

===Repair mode===
[[File:Building mechanics (ghost mode).png|thumb|right|150px|A standing torch created with ghost mode.]]
If a structure has visible signs of damage (at 50% health or below) or if the structure is below 100% health, players can fix it with its base material. For example, a [[square foundation]] requires one [[ash log]] if the structure is below 100%. 

Players will need to ensure the structure's health stays above 1%. Otherwise, the structure will collapse, leaving behind the base materials used to build it.

===Ghost mode===
[[File:Building mechanics (cycle snapping mode, basic).png|thumb|right|A structure with the most critical points of contact.]]
Players can create ghost-like structures without the required materials, either on a solid foundation or a wall. Ghost mode is useful for determining whether an object can be stable without building with physical materials on hand. After placing the object, this creates a pseudo-structure that can be built whenever the player has the required materials. To destroy the pseudo-structure, players can go to their build menu, toggle "Repair mode", and click the scroll wheel to dismantle the structure. To build the pseudo-structure, click on the {{Key press|CTRL}} key.

Ghost mode will not work in the temple at [[Temple Woods]], [[vault]]s, and inside instanced areas.

===Cycle snapping mode===
[[File:Building mechanics (cycle snapping mode, advanced).png|thumb|right|A structure with all of the available points of contact.]]
Players who enable cycle snapping mode can see either the object's full points of contact when connecting structures, the object's most critical points of contact, or no points of contact. This also works with ghost mode, as players can see the points of contact with the pseudo-structure. Cycle snapping mode will only be enabled if players are hovering over the previewed object with another built object. 

Note that only house structures will have cycle-snapping mode; any decorations, such as [[barrel]]s, will not show points of contact on their outlines.

====No snapping====
No snapping allows the player to '''not''' allow the object to be automatically placed to another built object. This may be useful for abstractly placing objects without the object moving automatically.

====Basic snapping====
Basic snapping allows the player to see the '''most critical''' points of contact. For example, a [[wall]] and a [[square tile]] will display four points of contact on each corner, and a floor will also display four points of contact

====Advanced snapping====
Advanced snapping allows the player to see '''all''' of the points of contact. For example, a wall and a square tile will display 13 points of contact, with three between the corners.

==Stability==
Objects that do not have a solid foundation underneath will display a yellow outline (warning) around the previewed object and a red outline (prohibited) around the previewed object. Certain structures, such as a wall or floor, can be built up to six structures above the ground without a foundation. In addition, directly stacking objects above each other will perform the same action, depending on the constructed object. For larger constructions, using multiple foundations on the ground is necessary to expand the stable building area. This also adds redundancy, preventing a total collapse if one anchor is accidentally removed.

Areas with non-stable foundations include the temple at Temple Woods, vaults, and inside instanced areas.

When placing a foundation or anything on the ground, all basic snapping points for the desired structure must be in contact with the ground at the same time. This means any structure (or the tent from casting [[Summon Shelter]]) must be on flat land. Otherwise, a red '''UNSTABLE''' will pop up on the screen.

===Block types and stability===
Beams and foundations are the best blocks to use for anchors as they provide the greatest amount of stability. Thick and thin beams offer the same stability and can provide the upper-constructed objects a stable defence if the bottom of the structure is broken. Walls and stairs, when used as anchors, provide less stability than beams or foundations.

The material used for the anchor block dictates the build's stability limits. Ash objects allow for a structure 5 blocks high and 3 blocks wide. The travel distance for stability is about 4-5 blocks from the anchor. Oak is a superior anchor material, permitting builds of up to 8 blocks high and 5 blocks wide. Stone and above provide support up to 7 blocks wide. It also provides a stable travel distance of 6-8 blocks without a foundation.

==General base building tips==
* Prioritise oak structures: While adventuring in Ashenfall, there are higher-tier materials that can be used to create bases. As you advance your Construction level, you gain access to higher-tier buildings and foundations, but these buildings become more expensive. To be cost-effective in terms of resources for a starter base in a new area/region, it is best to use '''Oak''' structures as the resources are quicker to acquire.
** You can also use the highest-tier material available to you, but it takes time to acquire a substantial amount of resources to construct these structures.
** In case you don't have enough resources to make a base completely out of Oak material, you can always use Ash without impacting overall stability limits.
* Beware of false anchors: A block may appear green and seem to be on (or in) the ground, but it might not be a true anchor providing its own stability. This can severely limit the player's build and may be related to a known issue of placing beams on cliffs. Be cautious when deleting any anchor to avoid an unexpected structural collapse.
* Use beams for framing: Beams are recommended for creating the main frame of a build because they make it easy to visualise and trace stability paths.
* Roofs: Roofs are often difficult to place due to stability limits at the top of a building. Plan to have less roof space, potentially reducing the building height by a floor or two to accommodate a decent-sized roof. Frequent support beams running up from anchors are needed for larger roofs.
* Leverage different beam types and sizes:
** Long vs. short beams: It is best to use long beams for the main structure, but supplement them with short poles where needed. Short poles can sometimes provide extra building room at their unique snapping points.
** Angled beams: Using 45° beams (or other angled beams, depending on the player's structure) can help expand the buildable area by filling in gaps between horizontal and vertical beams. They are also useful for anchoring structures into the cliffside.

Combat:
{{external|os|rs|rsc}}
{{otheruses|def=no|the music played during combat|Combat (music)}}
'''Combat''' is an event in ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'' in which two or more players and/or creatures fight. Combat is based around a randomly generated numbers in the form of "damage", which deplete a target's life points. The damage done by the parties involved is determined by several factors, including weapons and equipment.

Players can influence their effectiveness in combat in many ways, such as boosting their combat via [[perks]].

== Combat ==
The three combat classes in ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'' are '''melee''', '''ranged''', and '''magic.'''

=== Melee ===
* [[Armour#Melee Armour|Melee armour]] offers a -% in block stamina cost, +% in crit chance after blocking, and a +% on damage to staggered opponents on all three sets.
** Melee armour also has a greater defence against melee attacks, while having the weakest defence against magic attacks.
* Melee weapons have 3 damage types: '''slash''', '''stab''', and '''crush'''.

=== Ranged ===
* [[Armour#Ranged Armour|Ranged armour]] offer a +% stealth speed, -% in ranged attack stamina cost, and a +% to weak point damage on all three sets.
** Ranged armour also has greater defence against range attacks, while having a equal defence stats in magic and melee.
* Ranged weapons has one damage type: '''ranged'''.

=== Magic ===
* [[Armour#Magic Armour|Magic armour]] offers a -% stamina regen delay, +% magic attack speed, and +% in magical crit change.
** Magic armour also has a greater defence against magic attack, while having the weakest defence against melee attacks.
* There are three spell damage types: '''air''', '''fire''', and '''water'''.

=== Combat variables ===
There are several variables in combat that moderate an entity's performance. Life points are possessed by players and foes, whereas the other mechanisms are used in foes sparingly or restrictively.

* [[File:Health Icon.png|frameless|width=29x29]] [[health]] -  Health represent how much damage a player or creature can withstand. When an entity loses all its life points, it dies. A player's maximum life points is at 100. The primary method of recovering life points is either staying outside of combat for regen, or eating [[food]]. Armour also provides reduction to how much damage you can receive.
** [[File:Sangine Urn Map Icon (un-used).png|frameless|width=35x35]] [[sanguine urn]] - Sanguine urns are items found within Ashenfall that boosts max health by 10. Collecting them all would provide 310 total health.
* [[File:Stamina Icon.png|frameless|width=29x29]] [[stamina]] - Stamina represents how much energy a player has to be able to attack, dodge or block. If a player runs out of stamina, they will be unable to attack or dodge and blocking will cause them to stagger ([[parry]]ing can regain some stamina). The Primary method of recovering stamina is allowing it to regen on its own. There are perks that grants some reduction to stamina.
* [[File:Special Attack icon.png|frameless|width=35x35]][[Special Action|special action]] - Special action represent how much power a player has and can use. Certain weapons allow players to do special actions, where it would cost 25, 33, or even 50% of their special action energy.

=== Combat stats ===
Combat stats are levels that determines a player's benefit when fighting in one of the three combat styles. In ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds''',''''' players have three of the following combat style and benefits:

* [[File:Attack.png|frameless|width=40x40]] [[Attack]] - Per level, it decreases the cost of stamina when using melee weapons, and grants benefits at certain levels:
** At level 5 you unlock the ability to parry. 
** At level 8 you unlock the ability to use use weapon [[special action]]s. 
** At level 11 you unlock the spell [[Tempest Shield]]. 
** At level 16 you unlock the spell [[Weapon Expertise]].
** At level 20 you unlock the spell [[Enchant Weapon: Fire]].
** At level 23 you unlock the ability [[Adaptability]].
** At level 30 you unlock the spell [[Enchant Weapon: Air]].
** At level 30 you unlock the item [[whetstone|whetstone.]]
** At level 50 you unlock the spell [[Enchant Weapon: Water]].
** At level 99 you unlock the [[Attack cape]].
* [[File:Ranged.png|frameless|width=36x36]][[Ranged]] - Per level, it increases the chances of retrieving your arrows or bolts from enemies' loot when they die and grants benefits at certain levels:
** At level 3 you unlock the ability [[Quick Action]].
** At level 8 you unlock the ability [[Trick Shot]].
** At level 12 you unlock the spell [[Snare]].
** At level 15 you unlock [[weapon poison]] (called Toxic Behaviour in-game).
** At level 18 you unlock [[Hunter's Sense]].
** At level 22 you unlock [[weapon barbs]] (called Make 'Em Bleed in-game).
** At level 25 you unlock the spell [[Spectral Arrows]].
** At level 30 you unlock the ability [[Crossbow Trick Shot]].
** At level 35 you unlock the ability to create [[enchanted crossbow bolts]].
** At level 40 you unlock the [[Venomous Trapper]] effect of Snare.
** At level 45 you unlock [[fire oil]] to create [[fire arrow]]s
** At level 99 you unlock the [[Ranged cape]].
* [[File:Magic.png|frameless|width=37x37]][[Magic]] - Per level, it decreases the cost of stamina when attacking with magic and grants benefits at certain levels:
** At level 5 you unlock the ability [[Secondary Attacks]].
** At level 7 you unlock the ability to cast [[Water Magic|Water magic]].
** At level 11 you unlock the spell [[Surge]].
** At level 16 you unlock the ability [[Arcane Expertise]]
** At level 20 you unlock the perk [[Runic Refund]]
** At level 21 you unlock the ability to cast [[Fire Magic|Fire magic]].
** At level 25 you unlock the perk [[Afterimage]] from the Surge spell.
** At level 30 you unlock the spell [[Confuse]]
** at level 39 you unlock the item [[magical focus]].
** At level 44 you unlock the perk [[Greater Confuse]] from the Confuse spell.
** At level 99 you unlock the [[Magic cape]].
* [[File:Artisan.png|frameless|width=34x34]][[Artisan]] - Per level, it decreases the durability loss on [[equipment]], that includes weapons and armour.
** At level 56 you unlock the spell [[Magical Mending]].
** At level 99 you unlock the [[Artisan cape]].

==== Stamina reduction ====
Within ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'' there are method of reducing stamina when using combat from devouring [[Food|food or drinks]] that provide additional perks, such as [[Infusions]]. Infusions can be created by using the [[Cooking]] skill, and provides benefits such as stamina reduction when using one of the three combat style.

=== Combat Equipment ===
In ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'', combat equipment, such as [[armour]]s and [[weapons]] provide additional stats boosts to help you either do more damage, or reduce the damage you will receive. Using good equipment is essential to combat, as well as dodging and parrying.

==== Weapons ====
{{Main|Weapons}}
Weapons are items held that uses the either one or both hands to use and contributes on the player's base damage, damage multiplier and/or attack speed. Each weapon have a different [[power level]] that determines their stats. The higher the power level the greater the stats is. Some weapons, like bows and crossbows have their own base damage, which is increased when using ammunition, which adds a damage multiplier. 

Certain weapons, like [[black sword]] or the [[zombie axe]] have special effects that does better damage against certain [[Monsters|enemies]].

==== Armour ====
{{Main|Armour}}
Armours are items worn by the players that increases their defence against certain attack style, reducing incoming damage while providing buffs as well.. They also have a set effect which requires all three of the same combat style to unlock all three effect. Each armour have different power level that determines their stats. The higher the power level the greater the defence is.

==== Trinkets ====
{{Main|Trinkets}}
Trinkets are items worn by the players that grants additional effects to the wearer, such as the [[ring of recoil]], which deflects certain percentage of damages back to the attacker(s), or the [[salve amulet]], which increases damage to undead enemies. The [[ring of life]] provides a teleport back to your [[bed]] when your HP is reduces to 1.

=== Special Action ===
{{Main|Special Action}}
Most, if not all weapons have the ability to use a special action, this is an ability that allows the player to use the max damage of their attack, at the cost of their Special Action Bar. Some like the [[abyssal whip]] or the [[crystal bow]] allows a special attack that provides extra damage with other effects, like staggering or extra damages. A good numbers of weapons have special actions, they are

* [[Swords]]
* [[Greatswords]]
* [[Daggers]]
* [[Greataxes]]
* [[Warhammer]]
* [[Maces]]
* [[Scimitar]]
* [[Staves]]

=== Damage ===
{{Main|Hitsplat}}
There are different type of weapon damages, including buffs, they are:
* Stab
* Slash
* Crush
* Ranged
* Fire
* Water
* Earth {{Sic|Unreleased Damage type.}}
* [[Burning]]
* [[Bleed]]
* [[Poison]]
* Immunity
There are also [[Critical Strike|critical damage]], resistance damage and weak to damage, which both indicates when a target is receiving critical damage, is resistance to a damage type, or is weak to the damage type. 

====Weak spots====
{{Main|Ranged#Weak spots}}
Some enemies have spots around them that usually allow players to deal critical damage; these are called weak spots. Note that there is no cooldown for critical damage when targeting the monsters' weak spots.

==Trivia==
* In ''{{RSL|RuneScape}}'', as well as ''{{OSL|Old School RuneScape}}'' and ''{{RSCL|RuneScape Classic}},'' combat has a system known as the "Combat Triangle". A means to explain how a melee user beats a ranged user, a ranged user beats a magic user, and a magic user beats a melee user. In ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds,'' there is no system. Instead, the armour of each combat style provide defences against their counterpart, with the highest defence towards the same combat style they are from.

* Prior to 0.12.0: Armour also provided Lifeward, or Wardshield, acting as a shield of additional hit points. Newly crafted armour would have full Lifeward. After it was lost, it could be restored using [[wardstones]] or the [[Soul Food]] perk, prior to the perk being changed.

'''Commander Zilyana''' is a character who appears alongside the [[Scorned Wilderness]].{{CiteVideo|author=RuneScape: Dragonwilds|title=Scorned Wilderness - Narrative Trailer | RuneScape: Dragonwilds|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cA6J1J5s9X0|timestamp=1:50|date=10 September 2026|site=YouTube}}

==History==
''This section is a simplified explanation of their history. To learn more, check her {{RSL|Commander Zilyana|RuneScape Wiki's history page.}}''

===Pre-Ashenfall===
Zilyana is a {{RSL|Icyene|icyene}} from {{RSL|Hallow}} who arrived in [[Gielinor]] near the end of the {{RSL|God Wars}}, as one of [[Saradomin]]'s finest warriors, giving her the rank of Commander. During the war, she led the forces of Saradomin, even participating in the battle of {{RSL|Annakarl}}, defending it from [[Zamorak]]'s forces. She fought against their commander, {{RSL|K'ril Tsutsaroth}}, but was overpowered by the demon, mortally wounded and left for dead. Saradomin arrived to her aid and teleported her to a secret location, where he keeps the {{RSL|Stone of Jas}}. With it, Saradomin healed her so she could continue to fight under his name.

Sometime after the battle, Saradomin dispatches her with several soldiers to the {{RSL|Temple of Lost Ancients}} to assist a flock of {{RSL|Aviansie|aviansie}} that were delivering the blade of the {{RSL|Godsword}} and were pinned by Zamorakian forces. Arriving at the temple, the [[Armadyl|Armadyleans]], led by {{RSL|Kree'arra}}, were assisted by her and [[Bandos|Bandosians]] led by {{RSL|General Graardor}}. Although an alliance was formed after the sword was shattered to prevent K'ril from obtaining it, Zilyana would spy on all three sides, using amulets she received to listen in on their plans and manipulate the battle in her favour, although this did not last long. While all four sides began to fight each other, one of [[Guthix]]'s {{RSL|Guardian of Guthix|guardian}}, with several other druids, would cast a powerful spell to freeze the four factions, imprisoning the icyene in there.

During the late [[Fifth Age]], the prison thawed out, and the armies would continue to fight; Zilyana would continue her attempt to reclaim the sword pieces for Saradomin. Although sometime later, she learns that god of wisdom was evicted from Gielinor by the god of balance and could not return due to the {{RSL|Edicts of Guthix}}. But this would soon change when Guthix's resting place was discovered; she was amongst the factions' leaders to head there to slay Guthix. Despite failing to kill the god, as that deed was stolen by {{RSL|Sliske}}, Saradomin was still able to return, leaving the resting place with Zilyana to start planning for the return of other gods. In the [[Sixth Age]], Zilyana was tasked with doing other things, but she remained as the commander of Saradomin's forces, even escorting him to Sliske's {{RSL|Missing, Presumed Death|Grand Ascension}}, the finale of his {{RSL|Sliske's Endgame|contest}}, and assisting in the {{RSL|Elder God Wars|defence}} against the [[Elder Gods]].

When the Edict of Guthix was {{RSL|Aftermath|re-established}} by the {{RSL|The Player|World Guardian}} and their allies, Saradomin appointed {{RSL|Adrasteia}}, his daughter, as his successor to the Saradominist kingdoms. Despite disagreeing with this, she accepted it after seeing the wisdom in his choice, remaining in {{RSL|Falador}} to ensure her safety.

===Traveling to Ashenfall===
During her time on the mainland, Zilyana received guidance from Saradomin to head to Ashenfall and seek aid in stopping [[Kuldra]]'s attempt to destroy the world.

==Trivia==
* Her appearance is a strong mixture of her two appearances in ''{{RSL|RuneScape}}'' and ''{{OSL|Old School RuneScape}}''.
** The ''RuneScape'' influences are her hair colour being orange with white lines, blue attire having a Saradomin symbol, and her {{RSL|Saradomin Sword}}.
** The ''Old School RuneScape'' influences are the hairstyle, her wings being a blue gradient and having only one pair of wings, whereas in ''RuneScape'', she has two pairs. The metal plating on her shoulder and boots and she uses her iconic shield instead of a buckler.
** The ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'' unique appearance is the metal armor around her arm and her hip. In ''RuneScape'', they are leather, while in ''Old School RuneScape'' it is not completely covering her arms.
*** Another unique addition is the chest, having another metal plating, with a Saradomin symbol on it.
** In the trailer, she is missing her shield.
* In the trailer, she is called '''General'''.

Creative Mode:
[[File:Creative mode world interface.png|thumb|right|The interface for Creative Mode.]]
[[File:Creative Mode icon.png|50px|left]]
'''Creative Mode''' is a type of world that allows players to play in a world without any restrictions. It allows the player to have unlimited resources, undetectable by any aggressive/passive monsters, and roam the map to build and explore. Players can still fall to their death whilst in Creative Mode, but will not sustain any negative status effects, such as [[Poison]] or [[Wither]]. The character also does not need to upkeep any [[hydration]], [[sustenance]], or [[rest]], or otherwise experience interruptions to impede creatively expressing themself.

==Starting a creative world==
Players can choose the type of world upon opening the ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'' Steam client. From here, players can create a world and select "Standard", "[[Custom Mode|Custom]]" or "Creative". Players can create up to 8 character slots.

==Creative world features==
===Building===
* All [[buildings|building]] pieces will be unlocked.
* Buildings will not have any material costs.
* Players will have an infinite [[Inventory|carry weight]].

===Crafting===
* All crafting recipes will be unlocked.
* Crafting will not require materials.

===Skills===
* All [[skills]] will be maxed.
* [[Spells]] will not require [[runes]] or have cooldowns.
* [[Lodestone]]s will not have rune costs.

===Environment and survival===
* [[Sustenance|Hunger]], [[Hydration|thirst]], and [[Stamina|endurance]] will always be full.
* No world events will spawn (e.g., [[dragon]] attacks and [[Goblin Raids|hunted]] events)
* No aggressive [[monsters]] will attack the player.

===Stability===
Stability is tied to the type of foundation players use in their building; the better the material, the higher players can build. In addition, players can toggle stability '''on''' or '''off''' when creating a world.

==Settings==
===Building===
Players can enable '''No Building Stability''', where structures have no stability attribute, and players can build higher structural buildings. This setting is '''<u>off</u>''' by default.

===Environment===
Players can enable '''Friendly Fire''', where players can [[Player-versus-player|attack each other]]. This setting is '''<u>off</u>''' by default.

Critical Strike:
{{External|rs=Critical strike}}
'''Critical strikes''' deal an additional 25% increased damage from base damage roll (125% base damage).

==Mechanics==
The player’s critical hit chance affects the rate at which each attack can critically hit, dealing 25% more critical hit damage (x1.25). The base critical hit chance is 10%, and this rate (not damage) can be improved through [[perks]].

To calculate the damage multiplier of an attack or event, the following formula is used:

* For example: <math>(( 1 - 0.10) \times 1.00) + (0.10 \times 1.25)</math> indicates a 10% critical strike chance, no base damage boosts, and all critical strikes deal 125% damage. In this example (the baseline for all players), the equation would equal 1.025, meaning on average (true statistical average over many events) each attack deals 1.025x more damage per swing than displayed in the chart below due to critical strikes and base damage boosts.
The [[amulet of accuracy]] can increase the critical strike damage of [[Ranged]] attacks by 15%.

Currencies:
{{external|rs|os|rsc}}
'''Currencies''' are items that can be exchanged and are used for various transactions in ''[[RuneScape: Dragonwilds]]''. There is no main form of currency in the game, as only five known shops take different currencies. 

== In-game currencies ==
There are currently three types of currencies used in-game: 
* [[Soul fragment]]s, which can be collected within [[Fellhollow]] by killing [[undead]] or completing [[quests]] within the region and can be used in [[Death (Grim Reaper)#Death's Exchange|Death's Exchange]].
* [[Infernal fragment]]s, which can be collected within [[Dowdun Reach]] by killing [[Black Knights]], [[demon]]s or completing quests within the region, and can be used in [[Postie Pete#Evil Emporium|Evil Emporium]].
* [[Garou chit]]s, which can be collected throughout [[Umbral Sands]] and used to trade with merchants.

{{Game mechanics}}
Death:
{{external|os|rs=Death (mechanic)|rsc}}
{{otheruses|the death mechanic if a player dies|the Grim Reaper|Death (Grim Reaper)}}
'''Death''' occurs when a player's [[Health|hitpoints]] reach 0. Upon dying, a system message in the [[chat]] interface will say, "USERNAME has died". In a standard death, players can have multiple [[gravestone]]s and can retrieve their items at any time. In addition, players will retain their skill [[experience]]. In a hard mode death, players can only have one gravestone; not claiming their items from their first gravestone and dying again will delete all of the items in the previous gravestone. 
[[File:Death interface (message).png|thumb|right|The system message after dying.]]

==Respawning==
After dying, players in both normal and hard difficulty worlds will either spawn back at their claimed bed or the lodestone inside [[Wise Old Man]]'s temple if no bed has been claimed.

==Types of Death==
Players can die from the following:
* [[Combat]] from an enemy or another player with the PvP setting on
* Falling - either from cliffs or other high areas
* [[Poison]]
* [[Burning]]

Dedicated Servers: {{otheruses|general guide on setting up Dedicated Servers through Shockbyte and at home|setting up Dedicated Servers with Windows|Dedicated Servers/Windows|Dedicated Servers with Linux|Dedicated Servers/Linux}} '''Dedicated servers''' allow players to host persistent game instances of ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'', independently of their own game client. Players have several options for hosting their dedicated server, such as using [https://shockbyte.com/games/runescape-dragonwilds-server-hosting Shockbyte], a web-based option, hosting at home on their computer, or using cloud hosting. ==Hosting options== {| class="wikitable" |+ ! !Shockbyte !At Home !Cloud |- |'''Setup difficulty''' |Easy |Hard |Hardest |- |'''Price''' |Set |Depends on electricity costs/RAM |Depends on capacity |- |'''Game updates''' |Secured |Manual backups |Manual backups |} ===Shockbyte=== [[File:Shockbyte icon.svg|right|width=150|height=60]] ====Pricing==== Players can choose to rent a dedicated server on Shockbyte through [https://shockbyte.com/games/runescape-dragonwilds-server-hosting these manually hosting plans] listed below: {| class="wikitable" |+ !Pricing per month (USD) !Monthly !Quarterly !Annually |- !Ashwood (2 players - 3GB RAM) |$9.99 |$8.99 |$7.49 |- !Iron (4 players - 4GB RAM) |$14.99 |$13.49 |$11.24 |- !Anima (6 players - 5GB RAM) |$19.99 |$17.99 |$14.99 |} ====Configuration==== After purchasing a plan, players must enter configuration values. To do so, go to the '''config''' page: [[File:Dedicated Servers (ShockByte, 1).png|center]] Then click on '''RuneScape: Dragonwilds Settings'''. [[File:Dedicated Servers (ShockByte, 2).png|center]] More information about configuration settings can be found [[Dedicated Servers#Configuration settings|here]]. Optionally, players can set the World to '''one''' from their personal library. More information can be found [[Dedicated Servers#World management|here]]. Once players have set those values, write down the World Name and start the server. ===Hosting at home=== Dedicated servers will only run on a 64-bit operating system. Both Windows and Linux are supported, and the required RAM is 2 GB + 1 GB per player. The server can support up to 6 players, so the total required RAM is 8GB. ====Ports==== Dedicated servers use ports starting with '''7777''' by default (known as the '''Game Port'''), and the second server will use 7778 (known as the '''Secondary Port'''). However, players must ensure that the port(s) are reachable directly. This means the player's firewall, router(s), and ISP must forward UDP through those ports. You can edit the default port by passing -port=1234 into your RSDragonwildsServer.sh execution. Please note the following: * Every router between you and your ISP will need port forwarding. * Some ISPs will prevent you from doing port forwarding altogether. Some will have admin tools that allow you to do it. Others will require you to contact their Client Support. * [https://Portforward.com Portforward.com] has a lot of details on how to forward ports. * If your server appears in other players' server lists but is not joinable, then Port Forwarding likely failed somewhere. ====Installing the game==== The ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds - Dedicated Servers'' client is free and available on Steam. Players can download the Steam product directly or use the following CMD command line: steamcmd +force_install_dir C:\MyInstallFolder +login anonymous +app_update 4019830 +quit Next, run the client via Steam, or locate RSDragonwilds.exe in the dedicated server product folder and run it. Players are strongly encouraged to add the following launch options when running: -log -NewConsole Players who enter this command in the Launch Options will see a console feedback window that tells them exactly what's happening on the server. To do so: #Go to Steam > RuneScape: Dragonwilds Dedicated Server. #Right-click and select Properties [[File:Dedicated Servers (installing the game, 1).png|center]] #Set the launch option to -log -NewConsole [[File:Dedicated Servers (installing the game, 2).png|center]] ====Ensuring versions match==== If the dedicated server is no longer visible, use the logs to verify that the current game version matches the dedicated server version. Mismatches are likely to occur whenever an update or hotfix is released. You can find the version your dedicated server runs at the top of its logs. [[File:Dedicated Servers (ensuring versions match, 1).png|center]] Players can find the client version in the top-left corner. Note that the version is formatted as such: [[File:Dedicated Servers (ensuring versions match, 2).png|center]] ===Hosting in the cloud=== Cloud server providers are pending and will be scheduled for a later update. ==Configuration values== Dedicated servers require several settings to be configured properly. '''Changing those values while the server is running will result in those changes being lost.''' Linux configuration values can be found under: Files > RSDragonwilds > Saved > Config > Linux > DedicatedServer.ini Windows configuration values will need to be copied from Linux and created in: Files > RSDragonwilds > Saved > Config > WindowsServer > DedicatedServer.ini Mandatory configuration values are: * Owner ID: this is your ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'' Player ID. It can be found in-game at the bottom of the Settings Menu. The server will not start without your owner ID. [[File:Dedicated Servers (configuration values).png|center]] * Server Name: the name of your server, no matter what world it may run in. * Default World Name: Upon startup, your dedicated server will create a default world. This configuration value lets you decide how it should be named. * Admin password: Anyone who knows this password can enter the Server Management tab in the '''Pause Menu > Settings menu'''. They will be considered as Admins until the Admin Password is changed again. You can see the list of people who used the Admin Password to access the Server Management screen by opening Files > RSDragonwilds > Saved > Config > Linux > DedicatedServer.ini. Optional configuration values are: * World password: This will supersede any password stored in the world. Can be left empty if you want anyone to join your world. ==Finding my Dedicated Server== To find the created dedicated server, go to the Public tab of the Worlds screen: [[File:Dedicated Servers (finding my dedicated server).png|center]] In the search tab, type the world name. Note that the world name is '''case sensitive'''. After a few seconds, the created server should appear. If the server cannot be loaded: * Check if the server and clients are using the latest version of the current game. Note that Shockbyte servers automatically restart to the latest server version. * Make sure the world name is currently running. * Ensure the mandatory configuration variables have been set. * Look at the console log to see if there are any errors. RAM errors may occur, indicating that the allocated RAM for home-hosting servers may be insufficient. ** Logs for the server itself can be found in C:\Users\%userprofile%\AppData\Local\RSDragonwilds\Saved\Logs as well, this may help with troubleshooting. For advanced troubleshooting, send these logs to ModMail on the Official RuneScape Dragonwilds Discord. ==World management== When a dedicated server starts, it loads the latest .sav file available in C:\Users\%userprofile%\AppData\Local\RSDragonwilds\Saved\Savegames. If the folder doesn't contain a .sav file, the dedicated server will create a default Standard world with the default config.ini values applied. ===How to: Move a world to my Dedicated Server=== When copying an existing world save to your dedicated server, '''''DO NOT CHANGE THE FILE NAME'''''. If you have already done this, either copy the world save file with the original name, or rename it BACK to its original name. Verify that the server is saving the world correctly by checking that character progress is maintained when leaving and rejoining the server, and that restarting the server keeps buildings and objects. The server will need to be restarted. If the server was started with an edited filename, progress will be lost. #Ensure your dedicated server is stopped. #Back up every file from C:\Users\%userprofile%\AppData\Local\RSDragonwilds\Saved\Savegames to a safe location (on the dedicated server drive, the player's own drive, or the cloud). #Empty '''all''' contents from the C:\Users\%userprofile%\AppData\Local\RSDragonwilds\Saved\Savegames. '''DO NOT''' delete this folder! #Copy your local world .sav file from your hard drive: C:\Users\%userprofile%\AppData\Local\RSDragonwilds\Saved\SaveGames to your dedicated server hard drive (separate from the C: drive)RSDragonwilds/Saved/Savegames. #Start the server. ===How to: Create a new world with custom settings=== #Run your local RuneScape: Dragonwilds via Steam. #Create a new world with all the custom settings you need (Standard, Custom, Creative, etc). #Enter the world and make sure the player's surrounding textures are loaded (wait approximately 1–2 minutes). #Exit the world by pressing the {{Key press|ESC}} and clicking on Exit Game. #Back up every file from RSDragonwilds/Saved/Savegames to a safe location (on the dedicated server drive, your own drive, or the cloud). #Empty '''all''' contents from the C:\Users\%userprofile%\AppData\Local\RSDragonwilds\Saved\Savegames. '''DO NOT''' delete this folder! #Copy your local world .sav file from your hard drive: C:\Users\%userprofile%\AppData\Local\RSDragonwilds\Saved\SaveGames to your dedicated server hard drive (separate from the C: drive)RSDragonwilds/Saved/Savegames. #Start the server. ===How to: Back up saves=== It is '''very''' important to back up saves before updating your current dedicated server to the latest update. Please see the following to ensure you can save your archived saves: #Go to RSDragonwilds/Saved/Savegames #Copy any world save you want to back up elsewhere on the dedicated server drive, on your personal computer, or in the cloud. #You can rename the files to include the backup save in their names to make things simpler. ==User management== Dedicated servers divides users into three categories: {| class="wikitable" !Role !Assigning !Permissions |- |Owner |Player ID matching the Owner ID set in config |Can ban/unban anyone offline or online. |- |Admin |Players with the admin password (can enter in the Server Management page) |Can ban regular players who are online, but cannot unban. |- |Regular user |Players who have the World Name |'''Cannot''' ban or unban any player, including the admins or the owner. |} ==Known issues== * Inviting a player to your dedicated server via Steam Invites doesn't currently connect as intended. * Changing dedicatedserver.ini values while the server is running will result in those changes being lost. ** You will need to search for the world file name in your server browser, not the server name plus the suffix (e.g., .sav) ** For example, if your world file name is Dragonwilds_World1.sav, you will need to make sure the world name value is Dragonwilds_World1. * The server binaries are not available separately from the game. {{Game mechanics}}
Dragon Equipment:
{{External|os=Dragon equipment|rs=Dragon equipment}}'''Dragon equipment''' is a set of [[power level]] 9 equipment obtainable from the rare drop table of the [[Scorned Wilderness]] raid. These items cannot be crafted and does not lose [[Durability]] at all. Dragon items are made of a hard, dark-red metal called {{RSL|Orikalkum}}, a material from the previous cycle of the universe, from the home world of the [[Dragonkin (race)|Dragonkin]]. Orikalkum is known to be extremely hard to smith with, requiring dragon breath to melt the metal to bend it, which is how the equipment are made. Within the mainland, they use a different method of technique with an ore known as {{RSL|Drakolith}} to create a weaker version.

However, Dragon equipment are unique due to how they are crafted, requiring blueprints to even make a copy any of their design.

While this enchantment is applied, the held melee weapon will appear to have a silvery sheen with small wind breezes flowing around it and have their attack speed increased. This enchantment ''does not stack'' with other weapon enchantments, but ''does stack'' with [[Whetstone|whetstones]] and [[Lesser Attack Potion|lesser Attack potions]].

Currently, the [[Hitsplat]] is not registering every damage fast enough, causing one damage to stack over the other.

* Your melee weapon speed increases, combos that takes about 4-5 seconds, will take 3-4 seconds.
* When active, your weapon will do an additional 33% air damage based on your weapon damage.
** Example, you do 116 damage, the enchantment will do 39 damage.
** Special attacks/actions also becomes faster.

\sum_{i=1}^{L-1} \lfloor i + 300 \cdot 2^{i/7} \rfloor \rfloor & \text{if } 1 \le L \le 93 \\ 342,568 + \lfloor 52,560.5(L - 93) \rfloor & \text{if } 94 \le L \le 95 \\ 14,241(L - 95)^2 + 81,114(L - 95) + 447,689 & \text{if } 96 \le L \le 99 \end{cases} Following this piecewise function would provide the graph: {{Experience charts|type=linear}} ===Levels 1-93=== The first part of the piecewise function utilises {{OSL|Experience#Levels_1–99|''RuneScape''{{'}}s standard recursive notation}}, taking the previous level's experience and adding an exponentially growing term, using: \lfloor i + 300 \cdot 2^{i/7} \rfloor ===Levels 94-95=== Levels 94 and 95 are approximately linear, starting at level 93 (342,568 experience), then jumping to level 94 (395,129 experience) by 52,561, and to level 95 (447,689 experience) by 52,560. ===Levels 96-99=== ====Calculating the quadratic coefficients==== Levels 96 to 99 use the quadratic equation, f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c, where a is half of the second difference (a.k.a, taking another difference after subtracting the difference needed from level 95 to 96 and level 96 to 97). This is shown with the following: f(96) - f(95) = 543,044 - 447,689 = 95,355
f(97) - f(96) = 666,881 - 543,044 = 123,837
123,837 - 95,355 = 28,482
a = \frac{28,482}{2} = 14,241 ====Calculating the determinant (b)==== Since c is the starting value at level 95 (447,689 experience), use f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c and substitute f(x) for level 96 (with 543,044) to get the b coefficient: 543,044 = 14,241 + b + 447,689
b = 81,114, making the following function from level 96 to 99: 14,241(L - 95)^2 + 81,114(L - 95) + 447,689 ==Calculator==

Fight Cave:
{{External|rs=TzHaar Fight Cave|os=TzHaar Fight Cave}}
[[File:Fight Cave Icon.png|right]]
The '''Fight Cave''' is a dangerous combat [[Activities|activity]] located within [[The Burning Spire]], in [[Umbral Sands]]. It is introduced during the [[Quests|quest]], [[Icthlarin's Little Helper]], and is required to complete the quest's version of the cave before being able to do the real one.

==Location==
{{Map|Fight Cave|center=236096.12793,319442.578125|width=300px|height=300px}}

== Monsters ==
In this activity, players will be faced with [[KotHaar]] which each wave increasing in numbers and [[power level]]. Before each wave starts, you only have ten seconds to prepare your weapons and buffs. Every wave has between two to twenty different KotHaar enemies and may contain a mini-boss or two. Each wave will eventually have the arena itself shooting firebolts around the arena. The notable monsters are:

* [[KotHaar-Hur]]
* [[KotHaar-Ket]]
* [[KotHaar-Xil]]
* [[KotHaar-Kal]]
* [[Tok-Xil]]

=== Waves ===
During the quest [[Icthlarin's Little Helper]], the activity only has one option available: '''Trials of Fuzan'''. This acts as a tutorial for players with only ten waves to fight before fighting Fuzan. After completing the quest, the ability to fight in the full activity is unlocked. This will show up as "Start the Fight Caves" and make the player fight through thirty waves of KotHaar before fighting Fuzan. The final wave will have two Tok-Xil.

{{external|os|rs|rsc}}
[[File:Mixed_Grill.png|thumb|A Filling Meal, [[mixed grill]]. It is made with [[fillet]], [[haunch]], [[steak]], and provides the [[perk]] [[Meaty Meal]].]]
'''Food''' is a type of item primarily used to replenish [[sustenance]]. Some foods can be consumed raw, such as [[redberries]], but most food must be cooked to be eaten. A [[campfire]] or [[grill]] can be used to cook raw ingredients, and a [[stone range]] or [[cooking range]] can be used to combine ingredients into meals. Food with high [[sustenance]] to [[weight]] ratios will allow you to carry more while adventuring.

Most foods also provide [[health]], however, there is a 2 second delay between eating food, and consuming more than 100 [[sustenance]] will start to build [[Over Eating]] - eating 200 [[sustenance]] over the cap will trigger the effect, preventing the player from eating any additional food for 15 seconds. Because of this, when looking for ideal healing foods, food with higher [[health]] to [[sustenance]] ratios should be preferred, and not just which food heals the most. Additionally, food with higher [[health]] to [[weight]] ratios will also allow you to carry more while adventuring.

Some foods also provide [[perks]], useful effects such as [[Knowledgable Nourishment]], which increases the player's [[experience]] gain in all [[skills]] by 10%. The duration of these perks can be reset with the use of [[Internal Alchemy]], but the player can only maintain one to three perk(s) from food. Any previous perk will be overwritten by the most recently consumed food. Additionally, only one source of food can provide the perk(s). For example, the player cannot eat two one-perk foods to have them both. However, the player can eat any other food that does not provide a perk without overriding the previous perk(s).

The default sort for the following tables is based on [[Ashenfall|region]] and [[Cooking]] progression, and separated into a table for food without [[perks]], food with [[perks]], one for all food, and then the facility lists for the [[campfire]] and [[cooking range]]. [[Burnt food]] is only included in the [[campfire]] facility list. Use the Header sorts on the relevant table to find the food you're looking for. For example, use the perk-less food table and sort by [[health]] to [[sustenance]] Ratio to find food that will restore as much [[health]] as possible in a short time without triggering [[Over Eating]] or overriding any active [[perks]].

Gathering:
'''Gathering skills''' (or just "gathering") is a category of skills within ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'' that allow the players to interact with scenery items to acquire resources or materials.

== Overview ==
While these skills are strictly non-combative in nature, they allow the player to acquire resources that cannot be acquired in massive quantities in a short amount of time or not acquired through monster drops. These skills also have their own special type of tools that enable the player to get experience.

=== Mining ===
Mining is a gathering skill that pertains to mining ore nodes or certain rocks (such as stone boulders and granite deposits) with a pickaxe. At a high enough level, it is possible to acquire gemstones from certain ore nodes while mining.

=== Woodcutting ===
Woodcutting is a gathering skill that pertains to chopping down trees to acquire logs using a logging axe. By creating better logging axes using higher-tiered materials (such as bronze or iron), one can chop down stronger trees and weaker tress faster.

=== Farming ===
Farming is a gathering skill that pertains to growing and harvesting crops. By planting seeds in planters (or tree seeds on the ground), using watering cans, and compost, one can gather specific resources that would otherwise be hard to collect easier. At a high enough level, it is possible to create a higher version of compost and create a tool that creates a small increase to crop yields.

=== Fishing ===
Fishing is a gathering skill that pertains to catching fish in specific fishing spots. By using nets to trawl for fish closer to shore and cast using rods (with bait) to catch fish from far away, one can gather a renewable food source.

Guide for new players:
{{external|rs|os=New player guide}}

New to ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds''? This guide introduces the core gameplay systems, survival mechanics, and activities you'll encounter in [[Ashenfall]]. It provides an overview of essential topics – including [[quests]], [[skills]], exploration, combat, crafting, and progression - to help new players get started and build a strong foundation.

==Getting started==
To get started on your adventure, you must first purchase the game from your preferred platform. Here is a list of places where you can buy the game:
