Once you have purchased the game, launch the game and you'll be able to create your character, create a new world save, and modify settings. To create a character, go to "Characters" and decide which character mode you want to be. Know that you will be able to still create a character if you first clicked on play and entered whether on '''solo''' or '''online'''. Currently, there are three character modes:

* '''Normal''': A standard version of the game where you can play the game in a normal mode, access hard mode versions of the game, and play in public or dedicated servers.
* [[Custom Mode|'''Custom mode''']]: A version of the game that lets you customize the [[Worlds|world]] to fit how you want to play. It allows you to scale health, stamina, resistance, and even become invulnerable.
* '''[[Creative Mode|Creative mode]]''': A version of the game that allows you to play in a world without any restrictions, granting unlimited resources.

After creating a character and world, or joining a friend's world, you'll automatically begin the tutorial quest [[First Steps]]. Now, you can skip the tutorials, and the quest will have you meet the [[Wise Old Man]] in [[Bramblemead Village]], but it is advised that new players go through the tutorial to learn the basics of the game. Once you complete the tutorial (or skip it), you will then be able to start the first [[Quests|primary quest]], [[Dragon Slayer]].

==The basics==
[[File:Temple Woods.png|550px|center|frameless]]
''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'' is a game built on Unreal Engine 5 developed by Epic Games. Unlike its older predecessors, who use a custom game engine, this game uses real-time mechanics to run everything. Every in-game day is roughly 24 minutes, with a majority of that time (~19 minutes) being daytime. Actions in the game take different lengths of time to accomplish. For instance, freshly cut trees (if the stump remains) take roughly three in-game days (~72 minutes) to respawn.

To navigate the continent, there is a [[compass]] in the top-middle section of your HUD/UI. This will show you nearby [[Dragonkin Vault|dragonkin vaults]], [[Kebbit Burrow|kebbit burrows]], claimed beds, and player markers (both placed on the World Map and player indicators). All distances in the game are indicated as "meters" or "XXXXm" to inform you of how far you are from specific points, including your claimed bed.

To access your [[Map|World Map]], use the (default: M) key or (default: view) button. This shows all the locations you have discovered while leaving the rest covered in grey fog.

To travel fast throughout the continent, and even access newly discovered regions, players must unlock the building recipe for [[Lodestone|lodestones]]. To unlock this recipe, players must first acquire a [[Vault Core|vault core]] in a vault.

==Starting out==
After creating your first character and world, you will appear inside of a ruined temple in the temple woods sub-region of [[Brynmoor]]. The [[Lodestone (Inactive)|lodestone]] behind you is inactive until you either place your first lodestone or discover another lodestone. Aside from you in this temple, there is one other person there: the [[Wise Old Man]]. Speak to him to continue the tutorial quest or skip it entirely and meet him in the nearby [[Bramblemead Village]]. ''It is highly recommended for first-time players of this game to continue the tutorial instead of skipping it as it will help you get used to the game mechanics.''

For combat, there are small kebbits, swift deer, violent goblins, and beefy cows in this region that you can kill. For skilling, interact with special hotspots (Fishing/Agility), build plots (Farming), or chop trees (Woodcutting) to gain experience.

===Quests===
[[Quests]] can help you understand the game's story and explore, like ''First Steps'' and ''Dragon Slayer'', which help you adventure deeper into the continent of Ashenfall or unlock special mechanics like ''[[The Wild Hunt]]''. There are '''three''' types of quests that can be completed in the game: '''Primary''', '''Secondary''', and '''Tertiary'''. Both Primary and Secondary quests offer tutorials (ex: ''First Steps'' and ''[[Shrimp Catcher]]'', respectively), but Tertiary quests can only be completed ''during'' Primary quests. The only quest, before the full release, to feature Tertiary quests was [[Icthlarin's Little Helper]].
[[File:Imaru drinking from the river of souls.png|550px|center|frameless]]

===Lore Scraps===
[[Lore Scraps]] help you understand and learn Ashenfall's history, as well as Gielinor's. These scraps can be found in the [[Journal]] interface, where you can read all the items and lore scraps you find.

===Skills===
[[Skills]] are essential in the game as they give the character passive [[Perks|buffs]] (ex: less stamina used during sprinting), unlock skill-specific recipes (ex: angler's hat), or enable usage of powerful skill spells (ex: [[windstep]]). While skills do not actively allow you to gain access to specific regions of the game (like Fellhollow), they ''do'' allow you to access fast travel outside of lodestones.

===Exploration===
Players will start with the basic [[adventurer's tunic]] and [[adventurer's leggings]] as their armour and a simple [[torch]] as their off-hand.

The tutorial gives players their own weapons and starter tools made from loose stones and teaches them what they must do. In Brynmoor, the starting region, players can only acquire up to power level 2 gear before needing to head northward towards Ghornfell and unlock bronze and iron (power level 3 and 4, respectively) gear. Players who greatly explore the continent of Ashenfall will also come across [[Sanguine Urn|sanguine urns]], which can be interacted with to increase the player's total health pool by 10 points. While exploring the continent, you will learn over time the stories that take place here, or, if you like skipping dialogue, all the various monsters Ashenfall has to offer.

===[[Buildings|Building]]===
{{Main|Buildings/Mechanics}}
{{Youtube|Fgx65Mj_sCM}}
To start building, players will need a form of [[wood|lumber]] as their primary resource, as well as any other [[basic items]] that building structures, furniture, and decorations will require. Certain structures cannot be placed due to certain restrictions mentioned below.

Players cannot build:

* Inside vaults
* Either outdoors or indoors (depending on the structure)
* With no supporting structure below
* Higher than the structure's limit
* In most of [[Dowdun Reach]], save for places like The Courtyard.

====Build health====
Structures built with [[ash logs]] as the primary ingredient have 100 building health, whilst structures built with [[oak logs|oak]] and [[willow logs]] have higher building health. Defensive structures, such as the [[pallisades gate]]s and [[pallisade]] walls, have at least 2000 and 6000 health, respectively.

==Combat==
Ashenfall is full of creatures, some hostile, others friendly. From [[kebbit]] to [[Dragon|dragons]], killing monsters provides [[combat]] [[experience]] and useful loots. Certain monsters have a [[power level]] tied to the [[Ashenfall|region]] they are in. For example, [[Ghornfell]] is a power level 3 - 4 region, where monsters, such as the [[garou]], have a power level of 3 or 4. Here, you also have your own power level that greatly depends on the [[armour]] you are wearing. During and after the tutorial, your character will start with power level 0 armour and power level 1 weapons, like the [[Adventurer's Tunic]] and [[Stone Club]], respectively.

Killing monsters will level up the specific combat skill you used to kill, which is [[Attack]], [[Magic]], and [[Ranged]]. Here, the combat system relies on your movement (default: W,A,S,D) keys or joystick (if using controller), your primary action (default: primary left button) mouse or controller (default: RT) button, secondary action (default: secondary right button) mouse or controller (default: LT) button and evade (default: CTRL) key or controller (default: B) button. 

==Staying safe==
This game, while not purely multiplayer like its predecessors, ''does'' allow multiple players (4-6 players) to play the same world. Players can open up servers to the public, and some who join may not be completely good actors, so here are some tips to help you stay safe:

* Enable locked/private chests.
* Use totems to protect your builds.
* Set up passwords for your server if you want only trusted friends online.
* Make sure Gravestone protection is enabled, which will prevent players from looting it.
* Be cautious of trading in another world; be sure you are certain that the player you are exchanging items with can be trusted.

==What's next==
[[File:Fuzan Flying overhead.png|550px|center|frameless]]
Now that you have the basics down, here are some next steps to enhance your RuneScape: Dragonwilds experience:

* Set a goal, decide what you want to achieve, whether it is completing the first [[Saga]], building a structure or town, or gathering all the [[Vestige|vestiges]].
* Complete quests to explore new areas within Ashenfall, level up your skills to better gather resources!
* Experiment with the game; see how the game functions with different methods of builds, travel, or playstyle!
* Stay updated by keeping an eye on official RuneScape: Dragonwilds updates, patch notes, and announcements!
* Most importantly, have fun! RuneScape as a whole is about enjoying yourself, whether it be the survival game RuneScape: Dragonwilds, its MMO precursors - ''{{RSL|RuneScape}}'' or ''{{OSL|Old School RuneScape}}''!

==Conclusion==
There is so much to explore in Ashenfall, from quests to skilling and combat. Set goals, build smart habits with refilling on food, drinks, and potions, whack a few goblins if you can, and enjoy the tales to come. Remember to follow the rules of the game and respect other players. See you in Ashenfall and Happy scaping!

Health:
{{external|os=Hitpoints|rs=Constitution|rsc=Hits}}
[[File:Health Icon.png|frameless]]'''Health''' determines how much damage a [[player]] or a [[monster]] can take. Upon first arriving in [[Ashenfall]], players have 100 maximum health. However, scattered across [[Ashenfall]], there are currently 21 [[sanguine urn]]s that will offer a +10 permanent boost to health. The maximum health a player can have is 310. Health regeneration is negatively affected by having low [[sustenance]].

==Effects==
* Currently, the maximum amount of health players can have is 310.
* Every 25 sustenance will increase the player's natural health regeneration by 0.5/sec, up to a maximum of 2.0/sec, and a minimum of 0.5/sec.
** Health will regenerate after no player damage is taken for 11 seconds.

==Damage events==
Damage to the player can come from many sources, including enemies, falling a large distance, damage-over-time (DOTs), or the environment.

===Enemies===
Damage from enemies will scale rapidly based on the relative player: enemy difference in power level, and the player's defensive level against the used [[:Category:Damage Types|attack style]]. In addition, the published health on the monster pages assumes the player is wearing power level 1 armour. See [[Power level#Monster hitpoint scaling|monster hitpoint scaling]] for more information.

===Fall damage===
Falling a large distance will significantly damage the player, scaling exponentially to the distance fallen. Jumping from 11 metres below will start to damage the player by one to two hitpoints.

* [[Leggings of lightness]] is the only item to reduce fall damage.
* [[Windstep]] significantly reduces fall damage.
* [[Encumbered]] or player weight does not affect fall damage.

===Damage over time (DOTs)===
* [[Poison]]: Deals either 3 HP/s, or 4 HP/s, depending on the source, over an average of 8–10 seconds.
** Can be negated and protected against with [[antipoison]], or accumulation rate reduced with [[Fungal Fortitude]].
* [[Bleed]]: Once gauge is full, deals 30-32 damage in one second.
** The accumulation rate is reduced with [[Coagulated]] if the player eats a [[meat pizza]].
* [[Burning]]: Deals 4-8 damage over 6 seconds.
* [[Soulscourge]]: Once the gauge is full, it deals 10 damage over five seconds.
* [[Sustenance|Starvation]]/[[Hydration|dehydration]]: Either 1 HP/s for either 0 sustenance or hydration, or 2 HP/s for both 0 sustenance ''and '' hydration.
* [[Scorch]]: Works similar to Soulscourge.

===Traps===
Traps within [[dragonkin vault]]s damage the player when mistimed or overlooked.  These include: [[Spike Trap]]s and [[spear trap]]s. Ways to avoid taking damage include casting the [[Windstep]] if there is enough overhead clearance or timing the retraction of the trap.

==Death==
Death occurs when a player's health reaches zero. In a standard death, a player will appear at the last respawn point they set before dying (claiming a player-crafted bed for the first time, or the church at the start of the game if no bed is claimed), keeping their cape, all equipped armour, arrows/bolts, and runes at the time of death. All other items are placed in a [[gravestone]] close to the location of death. There is no time limit for the player to return to their grave.

Upon retrieving all items from the player's gravestone, the game will attempt to place the items back into the player's inventory in the orientation they were at death, placing items into the same hot-bar slots at the time of the player's death.
* Gathering any items during the run back to the player's grave will interfere with the game's placement of the items into the previous hot-bar locations.
* Dying before reaching the first gravestone will create a second gravestone working exactly as the first, if the player had items with them that would go into one.
* Upon death, [[sustenance]], [[hydration]], and [[rest]] will all be reduced. 
** Sustenance and hydration will be reduced by 10/100, unless the player is already at or below 35/100; in this case, they will be reset to the minimum of 25/100.  
** Rest will be reduced by 15/100, unless the player is at or below 40/100; in this case, it will be reset to the minimum of 25/100.
* In the event no respawn point was set by the player, or a previous respawn point was removed by destroying the claimed bed, the player will respawn in the starting chapel.

==Notes==
* Upon reaching 0 sustenance or hydration, the player will start taking damage until reaching 1 health; the player '''<u>cannot</u>''' die from having 0 in either of these attributes. This damage can stack with 0 hydration and 0 sustenance, making the player's health drop even more quickly to 1, however, this still cannot kill the player.
** Health lost with either 0 sustenance or hydration occurs at a rate of 1 HP/s.
** Health lost with both 0 sustenance ''and'' hydration occurs at a rate of 2 HP/s.

Hydration:
'''Hydration''' is a [[player]] attribute which determines how thirsty they are - if a player is low on hydration, their [[stamina]] regeneration will be negatively affected. To increase hydration, players can drink water or [[infusions]].
[[File:Hydration gauge.png|thumb|The hydration gauge as seen in game bottom left corner of screen]]

==Effects==
* The maximum hydration a player can have is 100. Attempting to consume another drink will make the top of its in-game infobox say, '''CANNOT CONSUME'''.
* Immediately after taking a drink for hydration, the player receives an invisible [[perk]] (buff) that stops the degradation of hydration for 60s.
** Interestingly, this timer begins upon clicking the drink and starting the [[Inventory|use delay timer]] of 2s, not after this delay is completed, as one would assume.  In this way, the buff is only 58s long + the 2-second use delay timer.
* Hydration status slowly dwindles over time.  When equal to or less than 25/100, hydration dwindles at half the rate:

{| class="wikitable sortable"
!Hydration level
!Dwindle rate
|-
|>25/100
|(1/11)/s, or 1pt/11s
|-
|≤25/100
|(1/22)/s, or 1pt/22s
|}
This means going from 100-0 hydration takes 1,375s (22m 55s).

* If the player has less than or equal to 25/100 [[rest]], hydration will dwindle more quickly (1s faster per point lost at base rate):

!Dwindle rate

|}
At this rest threshold, the player would instead go from 100-0 hydration in 1,250s (20m 50s)
* Every 25 hydration will increase the player's natural stamina regeneration:

!Stamina regeneration

* Upon reaching 0 hydration, the player will start taking damage until reaching 1 health; the player '''cannot''' die from having 0 hydration. The damage can stack with 0 [[sustenance]], making the player's health drop more quickly to 1, however this still cannot kill the player.
** At 0 hydration, the player will lose 1 HP/s.
** At both 0 hydration and 0 sustenance, the player will lose 2 HP/s

* Like sustenance, while at 0 hydration, the player cannot use the spell [[Eye of Oculus]]. This means when [[Build Menu|building]] large structures or player homes with the use of Eye of Oculus, hydration, and sustenance items are required.
* Like with sustenance but unlike rest, upon [[death]] hydration will be reduced by 10/100, unless the player is already at or below 35/100; in this case, it will be reset to the minimum of 25/100.
* After a full night's rest, hydration is reduced:
** 65-100: Hydration reduced by up to 40, randomly
** 25-65: Hydration reduced randomly by up to 40, to a minimum of 25
** 0-25: Hydration maintained at current value.

==Player Announcements==
Upon reaching certain thresholds of hydration, a player announcement on screen will display:

25/100: ''Your throat feels dry.  You could do with a drink of water.''

5/100: ''Your lips crack and your heart races from dehydration.''

0/100: ''You are critically dehydrated. Your body can't take much more of this.''

Interface:
{{external|os|rs|rsc}}
[[File:Interface - first spawn.png|thumb|right|A player spawning in a world for the first time.]]
The '''interface''', or '''user interface (UI)''', is the screen containing different buttons which, when clicked, display different pieces of information. 
__TOC__

Upon spawning in a world for the first time, players can see the following:

* [[Perks|Status]] - located at the bottom left of the screen and includes (from left to right):
** [[Hydration]]
** [[Sustenance]]
** [[Rest]]
* [[Health]] and [[stamina]] bar - located at the bottom middle of the screen
* [[Inventory]] bar - located at the top right of the screen
* [[Settings#Interaction|Quick action]] bar - located at the bottom right of the screen and includes:
** [[Chat]] - default keybind is the {{Key press|Enter}} key
** [[Map]] - default keybind is the {{Key press|M}} key
** [[Quests]] - default keybind is the {{Key press|Q}} key
** [[Buildings|Build Menu]] - default keybind is the {{Key press|B}} key
** Inventory - default keybind is the {{Key press|Tab}} key
* Aiming reticle - located at the centre of the screen
* [[Compass]] located at the top middle of the screen
* A sundial widget on the top right of the screen that will notify the time of day

==[[Inventory]]==
[[File:Interface - Inventory.png|thumb|right|The player's inventory menu]]
Players can access their [[items]] through either the hotbar on the top right-hand side of the screen or by pressing the {{Key press|Tab}} key on their inventory. After pressing the {{Key press|Tab}} key (or other key, depending on the [[Settings#Key bindings|key bindings]]), players can access their inventory and their armour slots. The number on the bottom right of every item indicates the current number of items the player has. All items have a stack limit and can be determined by clicking and dragging each item to another inventory slot. Items have a stack limit of 1, 25, 50, 99, or 999. 

In addition, a yellow bar indicates the player's weight. If the player goes over 400 (or 450 with the [[leggings of lightness]]), the bar will become red, and the player will become [[Inventory#Overencumbrance|overencumbered]]. The player will be unable to dodge attacks, run, or walk slower.

{{Game mechanics}}
Inventory:
{{External|os|rs=Backpack|rsc}}

[[File:Inventory.png|thumb|150px|The inventory weight gauge as seen in game bottom right corner of screen.]]
The '''inventory''' allows players to view and organise their collected [[items]]. There is a standard weight limit of 400 for the inventory which includes items in the players primary inventory, hot-bar, and [[armour]] slots.

Players, through levelling [[Agility]], can unlock perks to increase the weight limit by 75 units, to a maximum of 550.

==Effects==
* The inventory has 5 sections: 8 hot-bar slots, 5 armour slots, 24 primary inventory slots, 24 [[Runes|rune]] pouch slots, 24 quiver slots and 24 [[Quests|quest]] item slots.
* On death, all items stored in the primary inventory will be lost to a [[gravestone]] (see page for specifics of death mechanics); the armour and shield that are currently equipped will be kept along with runes and key items.

* Items in the primary inventory, hot-bar, and armour slots can be dropped, moved, or split via a key-bound user hot-key.

* Activating any usable item (such as [[Sustenance|food]], [[Hydration|drinks]], packs, or armour) places it on a delay timer of 2 seconds before an item in the same stack can be used again. 
** This precludes swapping armour sets rapidly, such as is commonly done in the ''RuneScape'' universe. However, with accurate mouse moments, armour can instead be clicked and dragged into the appropriate armour slot in the inventory, bypassing this delay timer.
** A stack of items, when used, will not open the stack, but just 1 item in the stack. To use a stack more rapidly (such as when opening [[goblin pack]]s or [[bird nest]]s), the stack can be split into separate inventory spaces. Each separate stack has its own delay timer which can drastically reduce the amount of time required.
** Items can also be used inside of containers such as chests.

==Over-Encumbrance==
[[File:Inventory - Weight Icon.png|thumb|right|The weight icon.]]If the player's combined inventory and armour weights exceed their carrying capacity, they will become [[Encumbered]].
* Encumbered players cannot run or jump, and move at 60% normal speed.
** Other speed penalties (such as using items or trudging through water) stack with the Encumbered speed penalty.
** This speed penalty does not scale based on weight (so 401/400 will incur the same penalties as 1000/400).
*Encumbered players no longer pick up nearby items automatically. The player may still pick up items manually, but this further increases the player's weight.
** The exception to this rule is the complete prevention of the player taking from bushes, or picking vegetables and flax, while Encumbered.
* The [[leggings of lightness]] are currently the only armour piece that increases the player's weight limit, increasing it by 50 (to 600 maximum).
** Depending on the player's Agility level, this can vary from 450 maximum carry weight to 600 max.
* The [[terrorbird mount]] can increase player's weight limit to 200
* If the player becomes too tired through [[rest]] depletion, the maximum weight decreases by 100 (to a base of 300).
* Encumbrance has no maximum limit; however, carrying more weight increases how many law runes will be consumed when utilising a [[lodestone]] teleport.

'''Queen Kuldra''', also known as the '''Dragon Queen''' and the '''God Eater''', is an ancient black [[Dragon (race)|dragon]] with five heads. She is the leader of the dragons ruling over the continent of [[Ashenfall]], and the current '''High Queen''' for some of the [[Garou (race)|garou]].{{CiteJournal|journal=Garou Highborn's Cloak|quote=Even after turning from the moon-goddess Lougrim, becoming servants of the High Queen Kuldra, the garou continue their ancient rituals.}} She is the boss of the [[Scorned Wilderness]] raid, and the final boss for Kuldra's Saga.

==History==
===Creation===
Kuldra was amongst the first dragons created by the [[Dragonkin (race)|dragonkin]] [[Lacrussa]] and [[Avisk]]. When Lacrussa was working on making a better race of dragons, Avisk would force himself into her experiments and suggesting to fuse certain dragons for a better results.{{CiteJournal|journal=Lacrussa's Ravings|quote=Avisk is like the scales behind my wings, irritating and in desperate needs of a good scratch. He keeps coming to me and trying to explain to me how I need to do X with the dragons, or Y with their eggs, as if he, an Aughra, has the slightest understanding of real science. Imbecile.}} He would mess with some of the brood, adding [[rune essence]] into the them.{{CiteJournal|journal=Lacrussa's Ravings|quote=He's already messed with some of the brood, tried to use that strange rune essence in ways that would cause energy to flow in certain ways. I can see the concept he's going for, but his clumsy nonsense just leads it to ruin.}} Despite Lacrussa's warning in trying to maintain a single headed dragons, Avisk ignored her, which led to several of these brood to die, all but one.{{CiteJournal|journal=Lacrussa's Ravings|quote=Trying to create some sort of enhanced mind for the dragons, as if they could exist like a swarm. All of them, of course, died. All but one, and she's turned out strangely}}{{CiteJournal|journal=Lacrussa's Ravings|quote=I encourage the growth of a single head for the dragons, keeps them sane and stable. There's no good that can come from multiple brains in charge of one body, yet she proves me wrong.}} Kuldra was born showing no signs of madness for having multiple minds. Instead she found that it would work as one, unified in a way.{{CiteJournal|journal=Lacrussa's Ravings|quote=All the minds work as if connected, as if part of the same whole. A single consciousness spread across all of them. A single personality.}} Lacrussa learns that the dragon was able to spread the rage across herself, weakening the effect, causing her to express other emotion and behaviours, such as curiosity, reason and even wit.{{CiteJournal|journal=Lacrussa's Ravings|quote=Because that’s what it is, a personality. A will. A mind of her own. She is enraged, yes, like all dragons are, but she spreads it across herself, weakening the effect. I have encountered curiosity, reason, even wit.}} This would make Lacrussa want to study her further, keeping her chained. During the study, they would get her off springs and conduct several experiments on them, exterminating the failures.{{CiteVideo|author=RuneScape: Dragonwilds|title=Scorned Wilderness - Narrative Trailer {{!}} RuneScape: Dragonwilds|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cA6J1J5s9X0|timestamp=0:37|site=YouTube|date=10 September 2026}} Kuldra would witness this, and slowly plot her vengeance.

===Dragon Rebellion===
After the [[Human-Garou War]], the [[Gods|goddess]] [[Lougrim]] donated her blood to the dragonkin for their assistance against the human and [[Bandos|bandosians]]{{CiteJournal|journal=Lacrussa's Notes|quote=One of them bleeds. Perhaps all of them, but this one for certain. She calls herself a goddess of the moon and the primordial hunt. Nonsense, of course, moons are rocks floating in the emptiness and there's nothing spiritual or metaphysical about a predator seeking lunch. Still, if I can refine this power? If I can merge it with a dragon, perhaps… just perhaps… I can turn these worthless dragons into something we can use.}}{{CiteJournal|journal=Sanguine Urn|quote=The dragonkin discovered a unique and powerful resources in their time on Ashenfall, the blood of a goddess - Lougrim. She was a moon deity, in-tune with the natural world, the forest and a source of great vitality. Her blood carries some of those properties.}}. Lacrussa would use this on Kuldra. After gaining Lougrim's blood, she would plot a [[Dragon Rebellion|rebellion]] against the dragonkin after seeing the continued abuse, despite their assistance in the war. At first, she was hesitant, but it was [[Velgar]] who convinced her and was the first to join her cause. When the rebellion started, Lacrussa was slain, along with [[Brakka]], from whom Kuldra stole powers for herself and shared them with Velgar, her most trusted ally,{{CiteJournal|journal=Velgar|quote=General Velgar was one of Kuldra's most trusted allies in the dragon rebellion. In the years that led to the betrayal of their Dragonkin masters, she would seek Velgar's advice on how to best handle the situation. His answer was always clear, brutality was the only language that their masters would understand.}} granting him his elemental mastery of earth.{{CiteJournal|journal=Fractured Cape|quote=Kuldra, the godeater, crushed him beneath her great claw and feasted on his anima-rich soul. Stealing Brakka’s power for herself. She gifted Velgar, her most trusted general, with the elemental mastery of the fallen Nodon architect.}} Before she could kill [[Rasthin]], the dragonkin, activated the [[Harmonic Resonator]] in hope to destroy Kuldra, only for the Dragon Queen to survive. In a battle that fractured the continent itself,{{CiteText|text=Leathery Parchment|quote=The battle was swift and bloody; their clashing energies created cracks in the very earth. The entire continent buckled beneath their fury, but only one of them could prevail.}} Kuldra then attacked Lougrim, who was protecting the garou village. Weak and wounded, Kuldra descended on her without mercy and devouring her body and taking her title of High Queen of the Garou. Some accepted out of fear, but others rejected her rule and left to another region. Having freed her fellow dragons, she sent them out across the continent to wipe out other settlements, other than the garou and [[Goblin (race)|goblins]].

Sometime during these events, Kuldra caught wind of [[Imaru]]'s and [[Xikotal]]'s mercy towards the human settlements in [[Fellhollow]], and as a result, she decided to confront the duo herself. As Kuldra descended on the region, nobles within the region would arm themselves in [[steel equipment]]{{CiteJournal|journal=Steel Platelegs|quote=When Kuldra arrived it was as if the air had grown heavy, pressing down on everyone. A whole village fell silent as the Godeater turned her gaze upon them. As Imaru and Xikotal rose to face her, villagers instinctively ran to don their heirloom steel armour, hoping that they wouldn‘t have to use it, but knowing in their hearts that they would.}} to assist Xikotal and Imaru, in the hope of defending their new home and bring an end to the Dragon Queen. Despite the help and numbers, they failed to bring Kuldra down. With Kuldra's strength and power seemingly unmatched, she would pull Xikotal's heart from his chest and devour it.{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Third Journal|quote=I have a new customer, and she won’t fit through the door.
Odd to empathise with a dragon, but I do. We all saw what happened. I watched as the great multi-headed dragon queen pulled Xikotal’s heart from his chest and ate it in front of his mate.}} She would then leave Imaru to grieve, as punishment for disobeying her.{{CiteJournal|journal=Steel Platelegs|quote=After Xikotal’s death, Kuldra left the region, leaving Imaru to her grief.}}{{CiteJournal|journal=Battered Diary|quote=She does not end Imaru's pain, not yet. She leaves her with the agony of loss and the dissolution of her dreams for the future. A cruel punishment, for the simple crime of peace. She dared to shelter the lost and wandering humans, rather than to put us to the flames.}} However, Imaru would challenge Kuldra a second time, after being infused by a curse{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Third Journal|quote=the rage of a dragon, combined with the power of a grief-curse, such a thing could be the blade needed to slit Kuldra’s throat.}} placed by [[Ravanna]].{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Third Journal|quote=Curses, though, that I’m good with those.

Imaru’s rage makes her the perfect focus. The beating heart around the darkest magics. She can be a weapon against the Godeater,}}{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Fourth Journal|quote=thought I could offer her something almost as good. I offered her revenge. I created a curse within her, using her grief and rage as a focus, so that it might strengthen her against Kuldra.}} However, this was not enough to even stand a chance against Kuldra, who killed her quite easily.{{CiteJournal|journal=Ravanna's Fourth Journal|quote=So Imaru died. Fell to the ground in a crumbled heap}} Despite Imaru's action, Kuldra had left the humans of Fellhollow alone, their fate met by the resurrected corpse of Imaru some time later.

With Ashenfall settlement destroyed, minus some of the garou and [[goblins]], Kuldra now rules the continent with her dragons.

===Sixth Age===
During the 14th Year of the [[Sixth Age]], while ruling unchallenged, an expedition had made its way to Ashenfall; her generals had attacked the expedition in her name. After the arrival of a group of [[Player Character|adventurers]], Kuldra would start gathering pieces of the Harmonic Resonator to cause another explosion that would devour the world. Before she could put her plan into motion and put an end to the world, the adventurer(s) made their way into her sanctum and, through a grueling barrage of her hatchlings trying to protect her from the intruders, was unable to survive after they destroyed her heart.

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|Kuldra's tale is tragic really. An innocent child, raised by monsters: tormented, tortured, and forced to create legions of children who were all taken from her and then either weaponised or dissected for future study.

She found comfort in the gentle warmth of a lover's embrace, only to see him taken from her by those same cruel parents.

Only one dragonkin ever showed her warmth, but their mind was distracted by thousand different timestreams and they could never give Kuldra the love that she deserved. A lack of love is like a poison: it seeps into one's soul and infects it with malice. You find yourself unable to believe that love could be real, and from it all the other positive emotions, such as charity, kindness, or hope.

Kuldra wasn't born a monster, but she chose to become one and she was determined to be the worst monster she could be.

For centuries she has gorged herself on the anima of Ashenfall, building her own power so that she might turn the region's wellspring into a weapon that would decimate the rest of the world. Why? Because the rest of the world is happy, and she needs to see that stopped. Now, she is dead - although her legacy will scar the world for generations to come. Hate breeds only hate, and Kuldra has had plenty of children.}}

* Her appearance from the concept art, banner image and the animated trailers shows some resemblance to {{wp|Tiamat (Dungeons & Dragons)|Tiamat}}, the goddess of greed and queen of evil dragons.
** Just like Tiamat, Kuldra is the Dragon Queen, has 5 heads of different types of dragons, has divinity in her and is worshipped.

* Within the lore of ''RuneScape,'' another dragon is known to exists with the title of Queen; the {{RSL|Queen Black Dragon}}, being the first dragon ever created, and is the ancestor to all dragons.
** Like the Queen Black Dragon, Kuldra is consider the first "perfect" creation, also had children, who were experimented on or enslaved by the dragonkin.
* Kuldra is amongst the few known dragons with multiple heads in the ''RuneScape'' franchise, with the others being the {{RSL|King Black Dragon}} and {{RSL|Verak Lith}}.

* Just like the King Black Dragon and Verak Lith, Kuldra's central head is that of a black dragon.
* She is the only monster in the game with over 10,000 health points.

This is a strategy guide to defeating [[Kuldra]]. Depending on the player's world difficulty, please refer to the relevant strategy section.

== Inventory Preparation ==
Kuldra is a [[power level]] 9 boss monster of the [[Scorned Wilderness]] raid.

=== Foods/Drinks ===
For your fight against [[Kuldra]], may it be first or multiple encounters, you'll want the following suggested items in your key bind hotbar slot or [[inventory]]:

* [[Stuffed Catfish]] which restores 200 [[health]] per consumption.
** It is suggested to also have the [[Undead Delight]] which restores 180 [[health]] and grants the [[Sea Life]] perk, regenerating 3 health every second 1,200 seconds (20 minutes.)
*** If you wish not to grind for Undead Delight, [[Eggs Royale]] also grants the [[Sea Life]] perk and heals 120 health.
* Use any [[infusions]] that buff your [[combat]] style.
** [[Infusions]] do not stack, so pick one that reduces [[stamina]] on your combat style action, or dodging.
** Or you can drink the [[Pumpkin Spice Infusion]] for the Soul food perk, to have it and Sea Life active. (Soul Food perk will not stack if it is from another food.)
* In the final phase, [[Antipoison Potion|Antipoison Potions]] can be useful. As the incoming attacks are new and the summoned mobs can easily combo a player out, [[Super Antipoison Potion|Super Antipoison Potions]] may be excessive, so the standard 300s duration can suffice.

=== Optional additions ===
If fighting in hard difficulty, or wanting to speed up the fight in normal difficulty, it is advised to have these items:

* [[Whetstone]] enhances any melee weapon held by +2 for ten minutes.
** In addition, lesser Attack potion can be added for the [[Focused Strikes]] perk for ten minutes.
* [[Magical Focus]] enhances staff and wand damage output from spell attacks by 15% for ten minutes
** In addition, [[lesser Magic potion]] can be added to increase the chance of landing critical hits with combat spells by 25% for ten minutes.
*[[Super Antifire Potion]] to grant [[Antifire]] perk to defend against her energy breath.

=== Runes and Spells ===
Although Kuldra cannot be attacked directly, her [[Dragon Hatchling|Dragon Hatchlings]] can. They have the same resistance as regular dragons.

You can also use spells to enhance your abilities against Kuldra.

* [[Surge]] would allow you to dodge attacks at a greater distance three times, costing no stamina.
* [[Tempest Shield]] for melee, crossbow and wand users, as it blocks more variety of attacks, even unblockable ones.
* [[Enchant Weapon: Air]] to increase the attack speed and damage of your equipped melee weapon if using melee.
* [[Spectral Arrows]] increases their damage done and is worth maintaining over the course of the fight if using [[Ranged]].

[[Internal Alchemy]] is optional to have, as it is able to refresh active food and drinks buffs, but only if you're willing to spend about 4–5 seconds of casting time, which can leave you open for attacks.

== Strategy Guides ==
[[Kuldra]] has a total of four phases, the first three requiring you to hit her with the device's blast a total of six times before she starts the next phase. Unlike previous bosses, Kuldra cannot be damaged by players themselves. Instead, Players must use the [[Anima Cannon]] to do enough damage on her before being able to enter her body and attack her heart. 

=== Main attacks ===
Kuldra's many heads will have basics abilities fired on you as you are charging up the '''Anima Cannon'''. Her main head will shoot a beam of energy out of her mouth across the arena. After that, at random, each head will begin their attack before she does her beam attack again. Green will spit a sludge of poison; Red will shoot 5 fireballs into the air, landing in random areas while one of them is targeted where you last stood; White will shoot a lingering ice shard into the arena where it will attempt to freeze the player; and Blue will shoot lightning at your position.

==== Dragon Hatchlings ====
During the first three encounters, a Dragon Hatchling will fly into the arena each phase and attack you. They are just like regular dragons, though exactly like the (Air Skeletons) that grant Anima, killing them will grant you the anima element they carry to either activate the Anima cannon, or activate the '''Anima Orb Dispenser'''.

=== Phase 1 ===
In this phase, [[Kuldra]] will use her main attack calmly, giving you enough time to dodge and plan your move. You'll first need to get rid of the blue dragon hatchling that will appear, as killing it will allow you to absorb water anima for the '''Anima Pylon''' and the dispenser. There is also a earth [[Crystallized Anima]] for players to use for the dispenser. You will need to use the Anima Orb on the cannon twice and fire a total of 6 anima blasts at her. At the end of this phase, all hatchlings will automatically die. [[Commander Zilyana]] will then appear and summon a barrier around her (like in the raid) for your protection. Make sure you hide within it or you will take rapid damage from Kuldra's special attack.

'''Note:''' You can carry an Anima Charge and the (Orb) at the same time, allowing Players to quickly gather the Orb and then deposit their Charge to reduce time spent waiting for new orbs to appear. Players also cannot carry anima orbs between phases as they will drop after Zilyana protects you from Kuldra's attack.

=== Phase 2 ===
At the start of this phase, you will be teleported to a new platform where you will need to repeat the same Anima Cannon process as before. Kuldra will start with her primary breath attack more aggressively and quickly, it is advised that you dodge and avoid them first before attempting to reactivate and use the cannon. Kuldra's red head attack will now do 7 spots of her fireballs; the green head will shoot two poison sludge at your previous position; the white will use two ice shards; and the blue will continue to shoot lighting (count the amount?). In this phase, a red dragon hatchling will appear. Killing it will allow you to absorb the Fire Anima in you for the pylon.  

If you have multiple people, you can stagger Anima deposits by doing Fire into the first Pylon > Fire into the (Orb Spawner) > Air into the second Pylon, then gather Anima as needed and create/carry orbs from there.  

=== Phase 3 ===
At the start of this phase, you will be teleported to a secondary floating platform. If you happen to have a lingering Anima charge from the previous phase, you can deposit it into the Orb Dispenser. From here, jump to the platform housing the Anima Orb Dispenser. Continue platforming across two more floating islands to reach the main arena platform. Be careful of the attacks from Kuldra's various heads, as (at least the Lightning attack) they can interrupt you mid-jump.

Upon landing on the main platform, Kuldra will immediately launch all of her main attacks aggressively and simultaneously. Focus entirely on dodging these incoming attacks for the first few seconds before attempting to set up the cannon or manage hatchlings. Hatchlings will spawn shortly after this initial onslaught as either blue or red variants (double check spawning priority).

This phase features two distinct Anima Pylons: Water and Fire.

* '''Water Pylon''': Collect an Anima Orb from the dispenser, insert it into the Water Pylon, and activate it. Doing so unlocks the gate leading to the Fire Pylon.
** '''Gate Skip (Optional)''': You can skip opening the gate by using the [[Windstep]] spell on the broken pillar to the right of the gate, then jumping over the stone wall. Note: You must be imbued with Fire Anima before jumping over the wall. To return from the Fire Pylon back over the wall, jump on the green gems located to the left.
* '''Fire Pylon & Cannon''': The Fire Pylon already contains an Anima Orb. Activating the Fire Pylon fully powers the Anima Cannon.

Once the Anima Cannon is online, load and fire it at Kuldra. After taking sufficient damage (6 hits), Kuldra will be stunned. A bridge will be created that leads directly to her platform, where you can 'Enter' the main head's mouth to begin the final phase.[[File:Kuldra Phase 4 Safespot.png|alt=Kuldra Phase 4 Safespot|thumb|'''Kuldra Phase 4 Tunnel Safe Spot''']]

=== Phase 4 ===
The final phase has you entering Kuldra's body and attacking [[Kuldra's Heart]]. In here, you will have to reduce the Heart to 0 hp, while handling the various [[Heartworm|Heartworms]] (do the Heartworms cause the Earth Spike attack?) that spawn as well as the Poison AoE attacks. Without the worms (verify if poison attacks only appear without worms), Kuldra can use poison explosion to damage the player, so it is advised that you use activate your [[Antipoison II]] buff and dodge. The lower her HP, the more explosions she causes. Additionally, keep an eye out for the worms as they do respawn. Once you see the hp reach 0, run to the exit as fast as you can. (specific ). There exists a safe spot within the tunnel entrance that allows Players to safely attack the Heart with ranged or magic, letting them avoid most of the poison explosions, with Heartworms rarely/occasionally spawning in the tunnel.

==Teleportation costs==
Teleporting between two lodestones costs an amount of law runes based on the distance between them and the amount of weight carried, with a minimum cost of one law rune. Note that the number shown on the lodestone map is calculated by the following:

<math>Law\, runes = (Distance\, to\, target\, lodestone\, \div 1000) \times (Total\, weight\, \div 1000)</math>{{CiteReddit|author=Mod Gifted|url=https://www.reddit.com/r/RSDragonwilds/comments/1wjwtf4/lodestone_cost_increases_with_each_teleport/pam9o8g/|title=
Lodestone cost increases with each teleport?|quote=Distance and carrying weight! There is some math behind it:
Lawrunes=(Distancetotargetlodestone÷1000)×(Totalweight÷1000)|date=18 September 2026|archiveurl=|archivedate=|notes=|name=LodestoneCost}}

For example, teleporting 8000 meters (the length of 2000 [[square tile]]s) while weighing 400 kilograms would require <math>8 \times 0.4 = 3.2</math> law runes which rounds to 3.{{Fact}}

Mount:
'''Mount''' is a mechanic that was introduced with the release of [[Fellhollow]]. It was highly requested by players who wanted a faster means to travel through [[Ashenfall]]. 
==Mechanics==
When on a mount, players can travel through terrain, and their stamina lasts longer as well. There are two base mount versions: the '''terrorbird''' and '''magic carpet'''. If the player is attacked, dealt damage, or is building up [[Wither]], the mount will vanish.

=== Types of Mounts ===
The list below are of the different types of mounts and their functions:
* '''Terrorbirds''': Terrorbird mounts are unlocked upon completing [[The Wild Hunt]]. Terrorbirds give +200 carry weight, making them good for travelling when gathering supplies.
* '''Magic carpets''': Magic carpets are unlocked upon completing the first section of [[Icthlarin's Little Helper]]. They do not give bonus weight, but do make traversing through [[Umbral Sands]] easier, and are much faster in the desert compared to other mounts. They are also lighter, taking less fall damage and allowing higher jumps.

== Ascension Upgrades ==
[[File:Mystic Forge Ascension.png|thumb|310x310px|The Ascension UI in the Mystic Forge.]]
Players can ascend their masterwork weapons and armour by collecting [[ascension core]]s through defeating enemies that drop ascension shards and creating them in the mystic forge or the cores directly through the [[Nightmare Crucible]]s. In order to start ascending weapons and armour, players will need at least 1 ascension core of the next power level available in either their inventory or chest along with a suitable item to ascend. This item must first be placed within the slot to ascend (it still stays in the inventory).

Ascending a masterwork weapon or armour piece consumes the core to bring it to the ''highest'' power level available to the player (<4 to 4, 4 to 5, 5 to 6, etc) and, if the player has multiple cores to reach the current highest power level in the game, the weapon or armour piece will require ascending ''twice'' to consume the cores needed to ascend to the highest power level in the game. It is worth noting here that weapons and armour that are already the ''highest'' power level ''cannot be ascended'' until a new major update.

Nightmare Crucible:
{{Stub}}

The '''Nightmare Crucible''' is a combat activity found within the [[Umbral Sands]] region of Ashenfall. It is meant to act akin to ''{{RSL|RuneScape}}''<nowiki/>'s {{RSL|Dominion Tower}} and ''{{OSL|Old School RuneScape}}''<nowiki/>'s {{OSL|Nightmare Zone}} in where the [[player]] fights against all of the toughest enemies Ashenfall has to offer thus far.

To unlock a Nightmare Crucible, the player must use a corresponding item, called an Engram, whose title matches the Crucible of interest. An Engram only provides a single attempt to a given Crucible:
- Single player: win or lose, the crucible will re-lock once the player enters it once. 
- Multiplayer: The crucible will only remain open as long as at least one player remains in it.

If the player dies while inside a Crucible, their [[gravestone]] will appear outside the crucible entrance.

The interior of Nightmare Crucibles are wide open, flat areas with almost no obstacles, save for the small Reward Pedestal in the center, and no safe spots for [[ranged]] or [[magic]] users. There is enough space to run around the arena in a circle and fight enemies from afar, but there is nowhere to hide. It is sometimes possible, depending on the player's positioning, to attract the attention of only a subset of the enemies in a given Crucible at a time.

== Rewards ==
Enemies in Nightmare Crucibles do not drop anything upon defeat.

Upon killing all monsters in the Nightmare Crucible, one [[ascension core]] is rewarded by interacting with the reward pedestal. In multiplayer sessions, additional players do ''not'' receive additional ascension cores. In general, one engram corresponds to one ascension core, assuming the crucible is cleared.

'''Parry''' is an unlockable ability at level 5 [[Attack]], where players can unlock the ability to parry incoming attacks to prevent damage, and [[stagger]] the attacker for roughly 3 seconds. Most enemies are staggered by different amounts, except for bosses such as [[Velgar]]. After a successful parry, there is a minimum delay of 0.550s where the player finishes the parry animation and cannot initiate an attack.

Perks:
[[File:Ferocious Fighter v1.png|thumb|The first, now deprecated, version of Ferocious Fighter. When active, Perks like this appear at the bottom left of the screen, to the right of the hydration, sustenance, and rest meters.]]
'''Perks''' enhance the [[player]] in one way or another, whether it be by reducing [[stamina]] costs or susceptibility to harmful effects, increasing [[Inventory|carrying capacity]], [[experience]], [[damage]], etc. Perks can either be [[Perks#Temporary|temporary]], [[Perks#Indefinite|indefinite]], or [[Perks#Permanent|permanent]]. Some environmental or enemy afflicted perks instead act as debuffs, reducing the player's movement speed, causing damage, etc.

==Temporary==
[[File:Perks Example.png|thumb|right|640px|The Perks Arcane Aligned and Frosted Flavours from Cooling Arcane Infusion, Knowledgable Nourishment, Foreman's Feast, and Soul Food from Glazed Pumpkin Sandwich, and Focused Casting from Lesser Magic Potion]]
Temporary perks must be activated or initiated and will deplete or end after a set amount of time.

* Regardless of equipment, the player can acquire:
** One to two perk(s) from [[infusions]]
** One to three perk(s) from [[food]]
** One perk from [[potions]] 
* While wielding a [[weapon]]:
** One perk from items, such as {{plink|Whetstone}} or {{plink|Magical Focus}}.
** One perk from [[spells]], such as {{plink|Enchant Weapon: Fire|pic=Enchant_Weapon-_Fire}}, {{plink|Enchant Weapon: Air|pic=Enchant Weapon- Air}} or {{plink|Spectral Arrows}}.

===Infusions===
* The duration of these perks can be reset with the use of {{plink|Internal Alchemy}}.
* The player can only maintain one to two perk(s) from infusions. Any previous perk will be overwritten by the most recently consumed infusion.
* Only one source of infusion can provide the perk(s). For example, the player cannot drink two one-perk infusion to have them both.
* However, the player can drink {{plink|Dirty Water}}, {{plink|Clean Water}}, or {{plink|Strong Tea}} without overriding the previous perk(s).

'''Player-versus-player''' combat, or '''PvP''', can be enabled for a [[Worlds|world]] when creating or editing one. When the option is enabled, players can fight each other, rather than just other [[monster]]s. 

==Creating a world==
<gallery mode="packed" widths="100" heights="100">
PVP Enabled Icon.png|PvP enabled
PVP Disabled Icon.png|PvP disabled
</gallery>
When creating a world, world owners have the option to turn on Friendly fire, enabling PvP for the world. The world owner can change this setting at any time whilst hosting the world. World owners must make sure to click on "Edit World" after making the PvP adjustment.

==Mechanics==
Players can attack each other whilst in [[Ashenfall]], [[vault]]s, or other instances (such as the boss fight with [[Velgar]]) through [[Attack|melee]], [[ranged]], and [[magic]]. If a player kills another player, the player who dealt the kill can access the player's [[gravestone]] and get their items. If a player dies and the world owner closes the world, the player who died will '''not''' be able to retrieve their items.

'''Poison''' is a status effect that environments and monster attacks can cause. Poison can be cured and prevented with antipoison potions. It will also naturally recover over time, though this can be dangerous as it will deal roughly half the player's health bar during the process. Inflicted Poison will do either 3 damage/second or 4 damage/second, depending on the source.

The perks [[Antipoison]], [[Antipoison II]], and [[Fungal Fortitude]] help prevent Poison buildup from the environment and grant some resistance to poison-based attacks.

==Sources==
* Monsters that can cause Poison status include [[putrid rat]] and [[garou druids]]. [[Velgar]] fires poison when the player is spotted during his random Patrols.

* Poisonous environments can be found in the [[Bloodblight Swamp]] and the [[vault]] within the swamp. Generally, the entire region will cause Poison to build up and cause continuous poison damage unless otherwise prevented/cured with potions.

* A [[melee weapon]] or [[arrow]]s coated with [[weapon poison]]

* Parrying enemy attacks with the [[dragonblight shield]]

==Monster hitpoint scaling==
A monster's base [[health|hitpoints]] can scale based on the region's power level. This hitpoint value is determined for all monsters in a region when the player enters that region, and the power level icon will change based on the player's average power level, determined by their armour. The formula that calculates the monster's base hitpoints is shown below:

<math>Hitpoints = Region\, Power \, Level\, \times \, Monster's\, Base\, Hitpoints</math>

Power level 1 monsters (e.g., [[chicken]]s, [[kebbit]]s, etc.) do not scale their hitpoints; those are always at their base value, regardless of the region's power level.

Saga:
{{Otheruses|major narrative arcs for the game|the list of individual quests|Quests}} '''Sagas''' are major narrative arcs in ''[[RuneScape: Dragonwilds]]'', told through the game's primary [[quests]]. Each saga follows a central storyline that unfolds across the continent of [[Ashenfall]]. Most regions contain a single chapter dedicated to their local narrative; however, '''Wrath of Velgar''' is an exception, beginning in [[Brynmoor]] before continuing into [[Ghornfell]], making it the only chapter to span multiple regions. == Sagas == === Kuldra's Saga === '''Kuldra's Saga''' is the first saga to be released alongside ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds''. It follows the [[player]]'s arrival in Ashenfall and their efforts to confront [[Kuldra]] and her [[Dragon (race)|dragons]]. It takes place during the [[Sixth Age]], following the events of {{RSL|Aftermath}}, and establishes the beginning of the player's journey across the continent of Ashenfall. ''[[The Story So Far]]'', is a [[Lore Scraps|lore scrap]] entry that provides an overview of the events preceding the start of the game. ==== Chapter 1: Wrath of Velgar ==== {{OccDur|Dragon Slayer}}
"They swooped down from the skies and decimated the landing party. Whole teams of people, gone, just like that. "Queen Kuldra bids you welcome," they laughed, as our comrades drew their final breath''.''" - ''[[Wise Old Man]]''
This is the opening chapter of '''Kuldra's Saga''', '''Wrath of Velgar'''. Upon arriving in Ashenfall, the player emerges from an ancient, ruined [[Temple of Saradomin|Saradominist temple]] and is introduced to essential survival techniques by several notable characters, including the [[Wise Old Man]], [[Doric]], [[Vannaka]], and [[Zanik]]. After completing this introductory training, the player sets out across the region of Brynmoor, battling [[Goblin (race)|goblins]] and other hostile creatures to acquire stronger equipment before confronting the dragon general [[Velgar]] at [[Velgar's Rise|his tower]] within Ghornfell. The chapter concludes with the player defeating Velgar and delivering his severed head to the Wise Old Man outside the tower. ==== Chapter 2: Beyond the Grave ==== {{OccDur|Withering Heights}}
"Welcome to Fellhollow. The whole region is infected with a terrible withering. Some dread curse that untethers the soul and drags it to the River Noumenon without ever sailing upon it, preventing the dead from moving on. This cannot stand''.''" - [[Death (Grim Reaper)|''Death'']]
'''Beyond the Grave''' is the second chapter of '''Kuldra's Saga'''. It follows the player's journey into the region of [[Fellhollow]] after the defeat of Velgar, here the players will be introduced to Death. Here, they will learn of [[Imaru]] and the plague she had unleashed within the region centuries ago and will be asked to slay her in order to restore the region. Here the players discover the [[Wither]] effect and how to enter it, and escape it. Players will be facing all kinds of [[undead]] when in the region, even [[green dragon]]s, preparing themselves before they face Imaru. The chapter concludes with the player defeating Imaru and the delivering her severed head to Death. ==== Chapter 3: Madness of Zamorak ==== {{OccDur|Black Knight's Fortress}}
"Full of angry Zamorakians. Quite the bother. Good thing you're here though, you can get us moving again. The way is blocked by something called the Gatekeeper. Not sure what it is, or who it is, but it's in the way. There's a nasty magical barrier before we can even reach them, but Doric's working on it as we speak." - [[Wise Old Man]]
'''Madness of Zamorak''' is the third chapter of '''Kuldra's Saga'''. It follows the player's journey to [[Dowdun Reach]] after the defeat of Imaru. Here, the player will be asked to help Doric unlike the barrier that blocked them from entering the next region. They'll have to located shards of the [[Dreaming Stone]] in order to restore it and undo the barrier. Players will be facing [[Black Knights]], [[mage of Zamorak]], [[blue dragon]]s and more in order to prepare and repair the stone and fight against the [[Black Knight Titan]]. The chapter concludes with the player's defeating the Titan and bringing his broken sword to Doric to prove their victory. ==== Chapter 4: Fire of Fuzan ==== {{OccDur|Icthlarin's Little Helper}}
''"Souls are coming to me from Umbral Sand at a faster and faster rate. My good friend Death informed me that the culprit is Fuzan, a dragon tyrant of these dunes." - [[Icthlarin]]''
'''Fire of Fuzan''' is the fourth and penultimate chapter of '''Kuldra's Saga'''. It follows the player's journey to [[Umbral Sands]] after defeating the Black Knight Titan. Here, they will be asked by [[Icthlarin]] to assist them in rebuilding his mother's mirror to lead them into [[Fuzan]]'s lair. The player will be tasked to gain the trusts of the Moon [[Garou (race)|Garou]] in order to gain the pieces needed for the mirrors. Players will be facing [[kalphite]]s, [[red dragon|red dragons]], [[KotHaar]] and other dangers within the region to prepare for their fight against Fuzan. This chapter concludes with the player defeating Fuzan and his [[Fight Cave|trials]], as well as delivering his head to Icthlarin. ==== Chapter 5: Rage of Kuldra ==== {{OccDur|Regicide}}
''"The lord of the skies has fallen, slain by Kuldra..."'' - Dragon Gate
'''Rage of Kuldra''' is the fifth and final chapter of '''Kuldra's Saga'''. It follows the player's journey through the [[Scorned Wilderness]] raid after defeating Fuzan and liberating the Umbral Sands from his tyranny. Here, they will be able to open the Dragon Gate north-west of Velgar's Rise and speak to [[Commander Zilyana]] to discover that Kuldra plans to destroy all of Gielinor by using strange discordant anima waves created by the Harmonic Resonator. This will force them to fight through hordes of [[Black Dragon|black dragons]], goblins, garou, undead, and solve puzzles using anima itself to bring the fight to [[Kuldra|the god-eater herself]]. This chapter, and this saga, concludes with the player killing Kuldra and delivering her head to Zilyana. == Future Sagas == It was revealed by [[Mod Dutch]] in the [[RuneFest]] reveal [https://www.twitch.tv/videos/2826225990?t=01h28m13s Twitch stream] that Kuldra's story isn't the conclusion for the of game, there are future sagas planned for the game. The next saga is planned to focus on a multi-year journey, one being to discover the ancient magic guarding the continent of Ashenfall and potentially revealing the continent to the rest of Gielinor. More information on this new saga will be revealed at [[RuneFest 2026]]. === Blood Crystal Saga === It has been revealed that the new Saga is '''Blood Crystal Saga'''[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HuEqe0JigCM], which will be introduced in 2027, more information will be revealed in RuneFest 2026. {{Journal entry|The dragonkin discovered a unique and powerful resources in their time on Ashenfall, the blood of a goddess - Lougrim. She was a moon deity, in-tune with the natural world, the forest and a source of great vitality. Her blood carries some of those properties.

If imbibed, even small amounts of blood, centuries old, can enhance one's vital spark, making you hardier and healthier. You can take more damage and survive greater threats, overcome the most dangerous challenges.

The blood was kept in a number of urns, which were separated and hidden across Ashenfall, in hope that the resource wouldn't easily be destroyed. It was to be a linchpin in their great endeavours, until Kuldra laid those lofty dreams to rest. Once they were buried, deep within the earth, but time, and other, more mysterious source, have brought them to the surface just in time for your arrival.

Anyone, and by that, I mean you, dear reader, can use the power of these urns for yourself. Explore Ashenfall and seek out these hidden locations; take the power of the goddess for your own.

Whilst the blood may be weaker than before, it will still make you healthier, increasing your ability to stand against the great threat of Ashenfall.}}

'''Scorch''' is a status effect that builds while in direct sunlight in the [[Umbral Sands]] and falls off in shade or at night. When the meter fills, it will drain 1 health and 1.5 hydration per second.

The [[Perks|perk]] [[Frosted Flavours]] from [[cactus water]], the Cooling [[infusions]], [[monkfish skewers]] and [[Umbral kebab]] and the [[armour]] [[desert hood]], [[desert robes]], and [[desert robe legs]] provide Scorch resistance. The more sources of Scorch resistance a player has, the longer they can remain in direct sunlight. The [[armour]] provide a bit better resistance than the [[perks]], but they all stack.{{Refn|There is currently a bug where having less than 5 sources of Scorch resistance, building some Scorch, and then swapping to 5 AND stepping into the shade will ''build'' scorch instead of lower it.}} The time a player can remain in direct sunlight before being afflicted by Scorch is as follows:

The '''Scorned Wilderness''' is ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds''<nowiki/>' first '''raid'''. This raid contains the Dragon Queen [[Kuldra]] as well as all monsters you have previously encountered.

In order to enter this zone, players will have to first complete the quest [[Icthlarin's Little Helper]] and start the [[Regicide]] [[Quests|quest]]. The entrance to the zone is located in the north-western area of the [[Fractured Plains]] in [[Ghornfell]].

== History ==
After arriving to [[Ashenfall]] long ago, the Dragonkin created a device called the [[Harmonic Resonator]] within the area now known as the Scorned Wilderness. The device's purpose was to gather raw anima for the Dragonkin, who would create an empire with it. Centuries after the creation of the device, [[Rasthin]] would activate it to destroy Kuldra, shattering the land. Kuldra survived, and now hunts for the pieces of the device to activate and lay waste to the rest of the world.

== Raid Info ==
=== Rasthin's Rest ===
[[File:Rasthin's Rest.png|frameless|width=370x370]]

This area of the Scorned Wilderness is the only buildable area in the entire zone. It is considered a safe hub, where players can build a base to return to when needing to rest, craft or repair. Players who make a bed here and as their spawn point will not experience any [[Warband Raids]], being one of the few locations that are safe from raiding and hunting parties.

===Dragontail Vines===
[[File:Dragontail Vines.png|frameless|width=368x368]]

Head into Dragontail Vines and head up the path. You will come across [[Runite ore]] deposits and [[Luminite Ore|Luminite ore]] deposits along the way, so it is highly recommended that you mine some up. In order to progress further, you will need to charge up an [[Anima Pylon]] with air anima. There is a floating crystallised shard of anima behind you to your right surrounded by three runite ore deposits. Siphon the shard and fill up your charge meter all the way to gain thirty seconds of anima infusion. Head back to the pylon and charge it using the anima you have to unlock the pathway to the next area.

Head down the newly formed anima bridge to the next area where Kuldra will appear along with Zilyana. Kuldra will begin attacking you with an elemental attack, but Zilyana will appear and tells you to get closer to her so she can protect you from the attack. Once you are close enough to her, she will save you from the ensuing attack and, thus, opening the way further into her lair. In this area, she will use an attack to inflict Soulscourge.

Head up the way to a white barrier. This will require you to charge up with Air anima once more, with another air shard nearby to siphon, in order to pass through. When you pass through, you will encounter a [[Black Dragon|black dragon]] along with some skeletal archers and zombies. Defeat them all to collect [[Discordant Residue|discordant residue]]. Aside from the residue, you will need to siphon some Earth anima next to pass through the barrier.

Once you pass through, head down the vine pathway to another area. This time, defeat the zombies in the area and siphon some water anima from a nearby water anima shard. Pass through the blue barrier and defeat the air-infused skeletal warriors to get enough air anima charged up to collect an orb from the [[Anima Orb Dispenser]] nearby. Go up the stairs and pull the nearby lever to unlock the path back around to the anima pylon. This pylon will require you to fill it up with anima again, but you can either fill it up with air or water anima to unlock the next area.

Go down the pathway and you will find a [[Zilyana Teleporter]]. Activate it and Zilyana will be able to take you back here if you choose the option "Fragments of Ghornfell" in the options. A small notification will pop up in the top middle of your screen saying that you have reached an extraction point.

===Fragments of Ghornfell===
Head further into the fragment and defeat the garou and goblins within the area. Once you have done that, head up the stairs to defeat another black dragon along with the garou thane, beserker, and goblin bodyguards. Once you defeat them, you will be able to use the central anima platform to attune to earth anima and unlock a nearby door. It is important to note that, beyond this door, lay a [[Sanguine Urn]] which can increase your total health pool by ten points. After collecting the urn, head back south down the stairs to continue through the fragment. There will be goblins and garou in this area, so prepare well. After clearing out all of the garou and goblins in the area, head up to the north-western tower and climb up the tower. Find a lever next to some thorny vines and interact with it. Chop up the vines too before going back down to the fire anima platform. Charge up your anima infusion meter fully and get up to the top of the tower within thirty seconds to acquire an anima orb from the dispenser.

With your new orb, head back down to the two anima pylons blocking the way into the next area. Use the orb on the broken anime pylon to activate it. Once you have done that, it will light up red. This means that, to open the way forward, you will need both fire and air anima. For the fire anima, head back to the platform mentioned earlier and charge up. As for the air anima, there is a graveyard nearby behind a barrier of water anima that you can use to lure the air-infused skeletons out of and kill to acquire a sufficient charge. Once you have charged both pylons, the way forward will open. Head into the church and turn left to fight against some skeletons, a necromancer, and an archer.

Clear out any enemies you see and head down the path. There is a route that is covered in poison emitters (like in the Bloodblight Swamp) and another path that is somewhat fragmented and covered in luminite. Either way will take you to a bridge that will lead you into an underground castle ruin. You will have to fight through numberous goblins, skeletons, some putrid rats, and an [[Abyssal Demon]].

'''Note:''' There is another Sanguine Urn in this area that can be acquired, but requires some parkour to get to. It is on the way to the Abyssal Demon.

Once you have defeated the Abyssal Demon, head out and you will have another extraction point. Activate the teleporter once more to unlock this area.

=== The Shattered Stronghold ===
Blocking your way into this area is a water anima barrier. Use the nearby crystallised water anima shard to infuse yourself with a sufficient charge of water anima to pass through the barrier. Once you pass through the barrier, quickly run to Zilyana as she will protect you from Kuldra's attack. Once the attack is done, head into the nearby doorway near the water barrier. Enter through the doorway and you will come across a fire-breathing gargoyle statue that will spew flames for a moment. To the right is a pathway to a crystallised air anima shard surrounded by rats and a PL 9 Rat King. It is recommended to defeat the rats here before siphoning the shard as they will attack you while siphoning. Collect enough for a sufficient charge and make your way up to the floor above where the gargoyle statue is and pass through the air anima barrier on the other side of the walkway.

After passing through the barrier, head down the stairs and pull on the lever first before engaging in a fight with the rats and Garou Thane. They will be charged with air anima which can be used at the nearby dispenser to acquire an anima orb for the pylon. Once you get the orb, head to the pylon to activate it. It will require fire anima to charge, so head around the crumbled tower to a breakable wall. Use your pickaxe on it to destroy it and head inside. Siphon the earth anima shard and head up the stairs and turn right towards an earth anima barrier. Pass through the barrier and use the lever nearby to unlock a shortcut back and defeat the garou within before attempting to siphon the fire anima shard as they will have a PL 9 garou thane among them.

Return to the pylon with the fire anima charge and it will open the way to the next area. As there is a black dragon in this area and some wild jade vines, it is recommended to deal with the closest jade vine so you don't get poisoned while fighting the black dragon. Once you defeat the dragon and head further down the path, keeping in mind of the garou and wild jade vines in the area, activate the teleporter.

=== Cataclysm Keep ===
Unlike in the previous areas, this area is more fractured and has less safe areas. Walk across the roots and small land chunks, minding the garou thane, and traverse through the shattered pathways to the other side. Once you have gotten through the pathway, reaching the other side, head through the doorway. This will lead you into a room with three vault guardians (two hulk and one sentinel), which can be easily defeated. Head past this to a puzzle that must be solved in order to continue further.

''In this area, you can find a Sanguine Urn. It will require you to solve a jumping puzzle in order to reach.''

After you activate all of the pylons, you will need to press the buttons in order for the path to be opened. The order is as follows: '''Air''', '''Water''', '''Earth''', and '''Fire''.'''''

Once you open the path, head up the stairs and reach the teleporter to activate it.

=== Kuldra's Sanctum ===
When you reach this zone, there are a few [[Runite Ore|Runite ore]] deposits along with [[Luminite Ore|Luminite ore]] rocks in this area as you reach closer to the Dragon Gate. Interact with the gate and you will be taken into the boss arena where you will face [[Kuldra]].

==Audio==
Players can adjust the Master, Music, SFX, and Dialogue volume. Note that all these options are set to 100 by default.

==Accessibility==

===Language===
Players set their language from its default setting, English (United Kingdom), to Spanish, French, Italian, or German.

===Font Size===
Players can set their font size from its default setting, Normal, to Large or Small.

===Enable Profanity Filtering===
Players can enable or disable the profanity filter, applying to in-game chat and players' signs. This can optionally apply to usernames and server names.

===Filter Usernames===
Players can check this box to apply the profanity filter (if set to '''enabled''') to usernames. Note that usernames will not be filtered in the server users list, so players can copy the usernames for reporting purposes. This option is set to '''disabled''' by default.

===Strong profanities===
This option determines the strength of the profanity filter if Enable Profanity Filtering is set to '''enabled'''. This option is set to '''Always''' by default.

* '''Always''' - will always filter entries, even if they are in the middle of a word. For example, if "cat" is in a profanity, then "scatter" would be filtered to "s<nowiki>***</nowiki>tter" and "catfish" is filtered to "<nowiki>***</nowiki>fish".

* '''Filter if full word" - will only filter entries that are surrounded by blank spaces or punctuation. For example, if "cow" is a profanity, then "coward" will be unaltered, but "cow" will be filtered to "<nowiki>***</nowiki>". 

* '''Ignore''' - will ignore the strong profanity filter list.

===Mild profanities===
This option determines the strength of the profanity filter if Enable Profanity Filtering is set to '''enabled'''. This option is set to '''Filter if full word''' by default.

* '''Always''' - will always filter entries, even if they are in the middle of a word. For example, if "cat" is in a profanity, then "scatter" would be filtered to "s<nowiki>***</nowiki>tter" and "catfish" is filtered to "<nowiki>***</nowiki>fish".

* '''Filter if full word" - will only filter entries that are surrounded by blank spaces or punctuation. For example, if "cow" is a profanity, then "coward" will be unaltered, but "cow" will be filtered to "<nowiki>***</nowiki>". 

* '''Ignore''' - will ignore the strong profanity filter list.

===Also filter German===
This option determines if the filter will also include words added to the German profanity list.

===Also filter Spanish===
This option determines if the filter will also include words added to the Spanish (Castilian) profanity list.

===Also filter Spanish (Latin America)===
This option determines if the filter will also include words added to the Spanish (Latin America) profanity list.

===Also filter French===
This option determines if the filter will also include words added to the French profanity list.

===Also filter Italian===
This option determines if the filter will also include words added to the Italian profanity list.

===Also filter Portuguese (Brazil)===
This option determines if the filter will also include words added to the Portuguese (PT-BR) profanity list.

Sixth Age:
{{external|rs}}
''This page covers the event of the'' Sixth ''Age of Ashenfall told in the [[lore scraps]], and is the current timeline of the game. For the full history of the world, click {{RSL|Sixth Age|here}}''.

The '''Sixth Age''' is the current age of [[Gielinor]]. It followed the [[Fifth Age]].

==Events==
The Sixth Age began with the death of [[Guthix]] by the hands of {{RSL|Sliske}}, which saw the return of the [[gods]]{{CiteJournal|journal=Guthix|quote=He was slain by the Mahjarrat Sliske, which brought an end to the Fifth Age and ushered in the return of the gods.}}, as the {{RSL|Edicts of Guthix|Edicts}} of Guthix were destroyed. It wasn't until a decade later that a group of powerful heroes forged an alliance and {{RSL|Aftermath|reestablished}} the Edicts.

===Dragonwilds===
It is in this age that the events of the game begin, with an expedition team setting off to explore the newly rediscovered continent of [[Ashenfall]]. However, the expedition team was attacked by dragons, wiping out most of team. The surviving team members, [[Wise Old Man]], [[Zanik]], [[Doric]], [[Vannaka]], and [[Cathan]], set off to explore the continent, setting up base camps as well as building a [[lodestone]] so new people can be brought in from the mainland. It is here where the game starts, with the [[player]] being teleported into the continent to help slay the dragons.

Spawning:
{{external|os|rs|rsc}}
'''Spawning''' is the in-game creation of an entity, such as a [[non-player character]] (NPC) or an [[items|item]]. Respawning is the recreation of an NPC, [[resource nodes|resource node]], or item, after its [[death]], destruction, or use. Despawning is the instantaneous destruction or removal of a resource, such as destroying a tree [[stump]]. The time it takes for an entity to spawn/respawn depends on the game's internal time mechanic. Respawn times shown in the wiki refer to in-game times.

==Spawning==
There are different spawning mechanisms, such as:

* After creating their character on the [[character creation]] menu, the player will spawn inside the [[Temple of Saradomin]]. 
* Summoning [[Velgar]] by using the [[challenge horn]] on the [[dragonkin altar]] at [[Velgar's Rise]]

==Respawning==
Several respawn mechanisms include:

* [[Monsters]] can respawn between one to three days, depending on the type of monster and their location.
* Several [[resources]] can respawn in their [[resource node]] between half an in-game day to three in-game days.
