'''Stagger''' is a [[combat]] mechanic where the [[player]] or [[monster]] stumbles and is unable to retaliate for some time. 

==Mechanics==
Stagger affects enemies differently, with this brief stun lasting either longer or shorter. Some enemies are immune.
An enemy can be staggered via:
* [[Abyssal whip]]'s special action will stagger non-immune enemies
* A [[warhammer]]'s special action will stagger non-immune enemies
* [[Parry]]ing an enemy strike

When either the player or monster is staggered after being blocked by a parry, the incoming damage to the attacker is dealt 25% more damage. 

The player can be staggered via:
* [[shield|Blocking]] while [[stamina]] is depleted.
* Attempting to block an unblockable attack (without the use of [[Tempest Shield]]):

Special Action:
{{External|rs=Weapon Special Attack|os=Special attack}}
[[File:Special Attack icon.png|left|frameless]]
'''Special Actions''', also commonly referred to as '''specs''', '''special attacks''' or '''specials''', are unique abilities offered by various weapons. Unlike [[Special Effects]] or [[Perks]], the player must choose to activate the special attack by pressing the Middle Mouse Button ({{Key press|MMB}}) / {{Key press|RB}} / {{Key press|R1}}. This will have your character perform a devastating special ability that deals extra or more damage as well as staggering them.

== Energy ==
Each special action uses a set amount of energy from the special attack bar, with the amount of energy used varying from 25 - 50 percent of the bar, depending on the special action. The energy bar regenerates at a default rate of 1 specs every second, requiring one minutes and about 40 seconds to completely restore. The energy bar is based on the player, not the weapon; changing weapons will not change the amount of special attack energy remaining.

Weapons:
{{external|os|rs|rsc=Weapon}}
[[File:Weapon Rack (Weapons).png|right|frameless|230px]]
'''Weapons''' are items that can be used to deal [[Health|damage]] to enemies or to other players in a [[Player-versus-player|PvP]]-enabled server. Their damage types are represented by the RuneScape combat triangle, and can come in 3 types - [[Attack|Melee]], [[ranged]], and [[magic]]. They are crafted via various furniture such as the [[crafting table]], [[blacksmith's bench]], [[fletching bench]], [[mystic forge]]. They can be repaired there as well if their [[durability]] drops or they break. The various foes in the world are weak to and resist certain types of attacks, so a varied arsenal is paramount for ease of exploration in [[Ashenfall]]. 

Various monsters and chests within the world have a chance to contain recipes for new weapons, which can be read and then crafted at their respective workshop. 

* See [[stamina]] for a breakdown of the stamina costs for using each weapon, or [[combat]] for a complete list of the damage per second for each weapon and style, enemy weaknesses, etc.

==Melee Weapons==
Melee weapons are currently split into two categories: one-handed and two-handed weapons.

Attack Combos shown include the bonus attacks awarded by [[Weapon Expertise]], unlocked at 16 [[Attack]].

==Ranged Weapons==
Ranged weapons are currently split into three categories: shortbows, longbows, and crossbows.

* Shortbows can be effectively used at both close and moderate ranges, but do less damage than their counterparts. 
* Longbows are very high-damage, long-range weapons, but difficult to use at close range. 
* Crossbows are one-handed and do moderate damage, but are only effective at relatively short range. 

===Shortbows===
Shortbows can either be drawn, or quick-fired with a reduction in range and damage. They have the lowest per-shot damage of the ranged weapons and moderate range, but the fastest fire-rate when quick-firing.

===Battlestaves===

Battlestaves can expend a large amount of magical energy at once through a secondary attack, based on the rune used. This consumes 5 runes per cast.
** Air: Stuns and knocks back enemies. Increases damage and stun based on charge time.
** Fire: Breathe fire in a cone in front of you. Increases duration, not damage, of the cone based on charge time at 2-5 ticks of damage.
** Water: Conjures a bubble of magic water that damages all enemies around the player when released. It then creates a field of magic water that heals allies standing on it over time. Increases both the first damage and the duration and size of the field based on charge.

'''Stamina''' is used for most actions, such as determining how long a [[player]] can run. Stamina is consumed from actions relating to skills (mining or woodcutting), attacking (melee, magic, and ranged), using special attacks, blocking, running, dodging, and jumping. It is displayed as a bar underneath the health bar at the bottom of the screen. [[Hydration]] affects stamina regeneration, and [[rest]] affects the maximum stamina a player has.     [[File:Stamina gauge.png|frame|The stamina gauge found below the players health bar]][[File:Stamina gauge limited.png|frame|A stamina gauge limited by rest depletion.]]

==Cost==
Stamina is depleted in varying amounts depending on the player's action.

* The maximum stamina a player can have is 100.

* All costs below are calculated <u>without</u> permanent [[Skills|skill]] levelling [[perks]] or other stamina reducing effects.
** To use a special attack, the player would need to be at least level 8 Attack.  This would give them five 1% stamina cost reduction perks from the Attack tree, meaning a special attack from a warhammer would cost: 40 x 0.95 = 38.
** Unarmed attacks are unaffected by skill levelling perks.
* After the player takes no stamina-requiring actions for 3s, stamina regeneration will begin. This is the base regeneration delay.
** The player can reduce this delay through perks, such as the 1/3 magic armour set bonus - see below.  Regeneration rates rely on hydration status.
* If a stamina cost were to bring the player below 0 and the player currently has >0 stamina points, the action will still be usable, and instead the player will be brought to 0.
** Although the stamina gauge only shows whole numbers, the gauge and calculations are actually decimal numbers.
*** The gauge value shown will always be rounded down; however, the decimal remains.
* Dodging can animation cancel most player animations in the game.
** E.g., a player can cast [[Abyssal Whip|Abyssal Snare]], and just as the cast animation completes, dodge to avoid enemy mechanics. 
*** This can outright cancel player actions, so timing is imperative.
* Stamina-reducing perks will '''not''' stack on each other if they are applied towards the same skill.

==Trivia==
* There was at some point meant to be 53 achievements for the game, but after a couple of small shadow updates before the release of Umbral Sands, the number was reduced to 45.
** It was first reduced to 50 achievements then again from 50 to 45.
* It was revealed in the update notes for Umbral Sands that achievements do not apply retroactively to all characters made before the update.
** Since the release of achievements, it is possible to gain achievements on both old and new character profiles, but only old characters will need to go back through to complete some achievements.
*Some achievements get added before major updates as shadow updates, thus making people unable to keep a full 100% completion of all game achievements.
*Prior to full release, there were a total of 48 achievements with two unobtainable achievements.

'''Tempest Shield''' is a [[Attack]] [[spell]] that produces an invulnerable shield for one minute that acts like any other equipped [[shield]]. However, this will release a powerful wind burst when the time ends if the shield is raised, knocking nearby foes to the ground. It can be invaluable before the player has access to stronger shields such as the [[iron shield]], since most stronger attacks will still pierce damage through shields before that, while the Tempest Shield will still fully protect the user even when barehanded (provided they are blocking).

It is recommended to always cast it before an encounter (as there is usually scarcely time to cast it once already in battle), as it can often be the difference between a close fight or an easy one. The invulnerability and knockdown can be vital in gaining an opening on an opponent, and using it even when not engaging with melee can be advisable, to leave open the option to back away on low hitpoints with a safe frontal shield.

'''Trinkets''' is an equipment slot item that allows [[Player Character|players]] to wears either '''rings''' or '''amulets''' to help them in training or in combat. Trinkets can be crafted on the [[Jeweler's Bench]]. Currently, only one trinket can be worn at a time.

A '''whetstone''' can be used to give a 15% damage multiplier on a player's equipped melee weapon for 10 minutes, and can be used in conjunction with damage-boosting spells, such as [[Enchant Weapon: Fire]]. Its recipe is unlocked after reaching level 40 in the [[Attack]] skill.

==Journal==
{{Journal entry|
The blade is not just a weapon in the wilds of Ashenfall, it’s a tool. Sometimes it’s the difference between seeing tomorrow and having a very bad today. 

Dwarves have always understood the importance of properly maintaining one’s equipment. They turned the care for their weapons into a ritual of almost religious significance. Blades would be cleaned, serviced and sharpened so that they might cut through deadlier dangers and challenge greater threats.

The whetstone is a simple device, but one that served as a backbone of this ritual. A smith would learn to gently sharpen the blade to the thinnest edge possible, treating it almost like a competition. They would boast and brag with each other about the sharpness of their blades. 

A popular dwarven myth speaks of the Prime Whetstone, capable of sharpening a blade to the point that no armour or metal could withstand it. Sadly, or perhaps thankfully, no evidence exists to provide any truth to the myth.
}}

Worlds:
{{External|os=World|rs=Server|rsc=Server}}
[[File:Worlds interface.png|thumb|right|The Worlds interface.]]
'''Worlds''' are separate versions of [[Ashenfall]] created by [[player]]s. Each world can have up to four players, and can have [[player-versus-player]] combat enabled/disabled. They can be played solo, opened to friends, or advertised on a public world list.

==Creating a world==
Players can create a world by clicking on "Create World", taking them to the [[Wise Old Man]]'s temple. 

===Selecting a world type===
[[File:World settings interface.png|thumb|right|The world settings interface.]]
Players can choose from the following types of worlds:

* Play solo - Players can choose this type to open a private world. Players can open this world type to friends whilst playing solo.
* Play with friends - Players can play with friends from their Steam friends list.
* Play with community - Players can advertise their world to the public worlds list.
* [[Dedicated servers]]

==Worlds==
Regardless of the type of world players choose, they can still choose whether the world is available only to the player, to the player's friends, or to the public. In addition, players can enable Friendly Fire, allowing players to have player-versus-player combat.

===Modes===
====Standard Mode====
Standard mode is the default option when starting a world. This will include only basic settings and difficulties, both of which cannot be adjusted after creating a world.

====Creative Mode====
{{Main|Creative Mode}}
Creative Mode is a game mode that allows players to play without any restrictions. It allows the player to be invincible, have unlimited resources, and roam the map to build and explore.

====Custom worlds====
{{Main|Custom Mode}}
Custom mode allows the player to set the difficulty and settings whilst playing the game.

===Settings===
====World name====
Players can choose a world name, limited to 16 characters. Spaces and special characters will still count in the 16-character limit and will be stripped out (e.g., -, ~, !, @, _, etc.)

====Difficulty====
Players can choose the difficulty of the world. The main differences between Normal and Hard are listed below:
{| class="wikitable"
|+
|
!Normal
!Hard
|-
!Hydration, sustenance, and rest
|Never reduces [[health]] below 1%
|Rates decrease faster and can reduce health to 0%
|-
!Skill XP
|Retained on [[death]]
|Skill XP beyond the player's current level is lost on death
|-
!Enemy attacks
|Deals standard damage
|Deals 15% more damage to the player
|-
!Death mechanics
|Multiple gravestones
|Only one [[gravestone]] can be active; dying again will make the oldest gravestone lost on death 
|-
!Weaknesses & resistances
|Standard weaknesses and resistances
|Weaknesses and resistances both increased by 10%
|}

====Friends worlds====
Friends in the player's Steam friend list who are also playing ''RuneScape: Dragonwilds'' will display the world name, friend name, players, type, PvP enabled/disabled, and last played, similar to the public worlds list. Ensure the world is not full when entering; otherwise, players will receive an error that the world is full. Note that setting a world to friends only will not be shown on the public worlds list.

====Public worlds====
The public worlds list includes the world name, the player who created the world, players online (of up to four players), the type of world (public or offline), PvP enabled/disabled, and last played. These can also include [[dedicated servers]].
